articles.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock
Many generative AI applications send the same long context with every request, and prompt caching avoids processing it again each time. That context can be a system prompt, reference documents, tool definitions, or the conversation so far. Open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock can reuse it across requests, which helps reduce input costs and response latency.
Prompt caching reuses the computed state of a matching prompt prefix, so repeated context is read from cache instead of being processed again. Amazon Bedrock manages the cache for you. Depending on the model, you can use implicit caching, which works automatically, explicit caching, where you mark the reusable prefix, or both. The more context you reuse, and the more often you reuse it, the more you can save.
As with other models on Amazon Bedrock, your prompts and outputs aren’t shared with the model provider or used to train models. For more information, see Data protection in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
Open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock now support explicit prompt caching. In this post, we use both modes with an open-weight model through the Chat Completions API and show how to read cache usage from each response. We then apply implicit caching to an OpenCode coding agent session on the same API and close with best practices.

I say Toronto-founded because the company quietly relocated to the US in 2023 to support its fundraising and IPO goals. Tenstorrent still has some 200 employees in Toronto, and hasn’t forgotten its Canadian roots. The Logic reported this week that the company has lobbied the federal government for sovereign AI contracts and funding for large-scale data centre buildouts.
Every company should be expected to make decisions in its own best interests. But Tenstorrent’s gentle tap dance back and forth across our southernmost border when it benefits them shines a light on a murky question: what makes a company Canadian?
Noting that the feds’ Buy Canadian Policy currently allows for, say, Walmart Canada, the policy wonks at The Canadian Shield Institute have argued for a revised definition in BetaKit. articles.title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons
articles.summary:
Out of curiosity, researchers at a small artificial intelligence lab in Accra, Ghana, removed the guardrails on their drug discovery AI model in 2024. They asked it to design toxins instead.
The model produced designs for 1,020 proteins and 5,000 small molecules. The researchers never made any of them in a lab, but software that predicts how poisonous a substance is scored all of them as likely toxic. Some of them resembled ricin, a deadly poison. The study was uploaded to the preprint server arXiv in May 2025.
“We were all shocked,” Darlington Akogo, founder of MinoHealth AI Labs, told Rest of World.
For Akogo, the results also raised a new question: If someone took designs like these to a company that makes DNA to order, would anyone stop them?
Across Africa, the need to regulate DNA synthesis providers is now echoing through the highest levels of government, Brenda Obuya, a senior official at Kenya’s Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, told Rest of World.
Akogo has traveled the world warning that AI poses an existential bioweapons threat. He discussed it on the sidelines of the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund Spring Meetings held in Washington, D.C., last year. He discussed the broader risk over dinner with Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates in 2023, whom he described as “on the fence” at the time. articles.title: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
articles.summary:
An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability, dubbed NoisyTCP, affects almost all Linux distributions and lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations.
According to Hyunwoo Kim, the security researcher who discovered it, this pre-authenticated remote corruption flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-99288) stems from a NULL pointer dereference weakness in the Linux kernel's TCP networking subsystem.
Unauthenticated attackers can trigger it remotely via maliciously crafted TCP packets that exploit the timing between SYN cookie handling and socket hashing to crash the kernel and operating system on targeted servers.
However, while CVE-2026-99288 exploits cause a kernel panic and take down the host, they don't allow threat actors to alter data or gain arbitrary code execution.
Kim added that although attackers can exploit this vulnerability against any Linux system that receives TCP packets directly and runs Nginx, Apache, or an SSH server, "the race window is narrow, so triggering it against a quiet bare-metal server can take a long time."
"Due to a race condition during lockless socket lookups, recycled socket memory can be accessed before it is properly initialized and hashed. A remote attacker could exploit this issue by generating network traffic that drives socket reuse, triggering a NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash that results in a Denial of Service (DoS)," the Red Hat security team explained.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Microsoft Rules Out Cyberattack in Outage, Warns of Phishing Campaign
articles.summary:
Microsoft says its recent Microsoft 365 outage was not caused by a cyberattack, but warns that attackers used the disruption to send phishing emails disguised as service notifications.
The November 12 outage disrupted access to Exchange Online mailboxes and Outlook. The tech giant also identified possible effects on services such as Teams, SharePoint Online and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Organizations and government agencies in several countries reported interruptions to email and other operations.
“This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents,” Microsoft said in a statement on Friday.
The company traced the failure to an earlier network capacity upgrade, with a subsequent network change exposing the problem. Microsoft said it fixed the underlying issue and was bringing services back in stages to ensure they remained stable. The Exchange Online incident, tracked as EX1550543, was marked resolved on November 13.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence said it observed a phishing campaign exploiting the disruption. The fake emails posed as Microsoft 365 service health notices and referred to EX1550543, the actual incident identifier.
In some messages detected on November 13, recipients were falsely told that emails held during the outage would be deleted within 24 hours unless they clicked a link to restore them.

articles.title: El sistema de IA de la FAA bajo la lupa: enfrenta preguntas tras el colapso aéreo más grave desde 2023
articles.summary:
La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) lleva años bajo presión por modernizar un sistema de control aéreo que opera con tecnología de décadas. Este año, la agencia dio uno de sus pasos más ambiciosos en esa dirección: contrató a una empresa de inteligencia artificial para rediseñar cómo se gestiona el tráfico en los cielos del país.
El resultado fue SMART, un sistema que prometía reducir demoras y cancelaciones, y que en cuestión de semanas pasó de proyecto piloto a herramienta nacional. Lo que nadie anticipaba era que su estreno a escala plena coincidiría con el peor colapso aéreo de Estados Unidos en casi cuatro años.
El viernes 13 de noviembre, la FAA ordenó la paralización total del espacio aéreo a las 3:54 p.m. hora del este.
El ground stop duró más de cuatro horas y dejó un saldo de más de 5.000 vuelos cancelados y al menos 827 desviados antes de las 7:05 p.m., según datos de Cirium citados por AP.
Qué es SMART y por qué quedó en el centro de la escena
El 10 de noviembre, la FAA extendió SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories) a los 22 centros de control de tráfico aéreo del país. Hasta ese momento, el sistema solo operaba como prueba piloto en la región de Washington D.C. desde septiembre.
SMART es una plataforma en la nube que analiza horarios de vuelo, condiciones climáticas, capacidad aeroportuaria y personal de control para anticipar congestionamientos y sugerir rutas más eficientes.

articles.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Agentic workloads are demanding more from inference systems. AI agents carry growing conversation histories across turns and generate a mix of reasoning, tool calls, and responses. Inference systems must support users at scale while remaining responsive.
MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 evaluates this balance between serving capacity and responsiveness using coding and enterprise workflows through API endpoints. During performance runs, generated tool calls and workflow intent are checked against reference values. Separate SWE-bench Verified evaluations assess end-to-end task-solving capability. These checks evaluate whether faster serving preserves model quality.
In MLPerf Endpoints v1.0, provisional NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 results show over 10x the throughput per kilowatt of provisioned power of NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 at a shared minimum end-to-end interactivity of 50 tokens per second per user.1
This post presents the benchmark results and outlines the hardware and software optimizations used in the submissions.

articles.title: Helping AI coding agents work smarter, for less
articles.summary:
At a glance
- Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches.
- TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.
- Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents. Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
AI coding agents are increasingly helping developers fix bugs and build features largely on their own, but every interaction with their models consumes tokens. In each session, an agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model. Most efforts to reduce this cost focus on individual tasks. Yet developers return to the same repositories, giving agents an opportunity to learn from previous work. Without that learning, an agent may repeatedly rediscover how to run tests, load tools it never uses, or spend dozens of turns revisiting the same error.
In our paper, TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents, we ask a simple question: can experience in a repository help an agent solve future tasks more efficiently? Will Indonesia ever win the Nobel Prize? That question probably pops into some Indonesians’ minds whenever Nobel season starts in October.
The reality is that there are no shortcuts to a Nobel. Breakthroughs recognised by the committee almost always stem from foundational work done decades earlier — often when it is impossible to foresee the practical payoffs.
Take the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel and Karl Deisseroth for pioneering optogenetics — a breakthrough technique that uses light to control nerve cell activity.

Interestingly, the road to optogenetics began with research that seemed to have nothing to do with medicine. Hegemann was initially investigating how the single-celled green alga Chlamydomonas swims towards light. His collaboration with Nagel eventually led to the discovery of channelrhodopsin — a light-sensitive protein that acts as an ion channel.
By 2005, Deisseroth’s team showed that channelrhodopsin could be harnessed to control neuronal firing with light. What began as a humble inquiry into pond algae laid the groundwork for optogenetics — now an indispensable tool for mapping and manipulating the brain.
This trajectory illustrates the road to the prestigious award: Nobel-worthy breakthroughs emerge from ecosystems patient enough to let basic research mature before demanding immediate benefits.

articles.title: Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement
articles.summary: In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis. In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. articles.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail applies that description to every request by meaning rather than by keyword. That same mechanism can also match more than you intend. A topic named Finance, meant to keep an assistant out of investment advice, also blocks “When does my direct deposit clear?”. Inputs close in meaning to the topic can get caught, not only the requests you intended.
When Denied Topics blocks too much or too little, the cause is usually one of four authoring patterns:
- Topics that block legitimate queries. A topic framed around a subject domain (Finance, Legal, Compensation) rather than the user’s intention can match queries semantically near that domain. This is a frequent failure mode.
- Topics that miss the requests they were written to catch. A definition built from keyword lists (“words like invest, portfolio, stock…”) misses phrasings that use other vocabulary and fires on unrelated inputs that happen to share those words.
- Examples that teach the wrong thing. Five paraphrases of one idea leave the topic’s boundaries unguarded, and examples that name specific countries, products, or companies pull those entities into the topic’s context.

NVIDIA cuPotential, a focused library designed for molecular dynamics, addresses these challenges. By offering modular primitives with a C API, cuPotential empowers developers and users to select specific components from multiple layers of the stack to accelerate workloads (Figure 1).
cuPotential provides direct space and reciprocal space utilities such as cutoff-based interaction evaluators and charge spreading functions. This release also provides a plugin specifically for OpenMM given its popularity in the developer ecosystem as an example. Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so you can get answers from tables through agentic retrieval. When a question needs data from CSV, XLSX, or XLS files, tabular search looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row in one or more tables or sheets. It then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer analytical questions that take several steps.
A finance team closing the quarter needs to know “Which departments must write variance commentary?” No single file has the answer. It depends on the variance policy’s threshold, the quarter-close memo’s budget revisions, and math over every department in the profit and loss (P&L) workbook.

For example, a Microsoft SharePoint site holds workbooks next to policies, and an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket holds CSV exports next to PDFs. - Source:

- Summary:

The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

Un responsable de Google a réussi à faire tourner Windows 11 sur le tout premier iPhone pliable d’Apple, avec l’aide de Gemini. Une expérience insolite qui transforme le smartphone en (presque) vrai PC miniature, au prix de quelques acrobaties techniques.
Voilà quelques années, déjà, que Microsoft a jeté l’éponge concernant Windows sur smartphone, mais il semblerait que tout le monde n’ait pas encore renoncé à l’idée. Ammaar Reshi, responsable du produit et du design chez Google AI Studio, vient de publier une vidéo sur X dans laquelle il fait fonctionner Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo, le tout premier smartphone pliable d’Apple. Pas de jailbreak ni de PC distant pour faire tourner le système, mais un projet développé avec l’aide de Gemini 4 Carbon en seulement deux heures, à en croire son auteur.
Windows 11 et iOS, une cohabitation assez improbable
Baptisé WindowsiOS, le projet ne remplace pas iOS, mais exécute Windows 11 24H2 dans sa version ARM64 au sein d’un environnement virtuel. Pour contourner les restrictions d’Apple sur la virtualisation matérielle, il exploite un moteur de traduction binaire capable d’adapter à la volée les instructions de Windows à l’environnement d’exécution de l’iPhone Duo. Une opération facilitée par l’architecture ARM64 commune au système de Microsoft et à la puce A20 Pro du smartphone.

articles.title: What Is Acoustic Micro Imaging? A Quick Guide To This Inspection Process
articles.summary:
Obtaining clear images of gaps and delaminations in advanced packages.
We all know how important inspection is for advanced packaging. Not only are these processes critical for ensuring higher yield, but they’re also integral for maintaining device reliability. As the industry pushes for smaller features and tighter spacing, even the smallest defects can pose major challenges. For instance, delaminations and air gaps can be detrimental in a market that demands increasingly complex devices. Such defects will lead to electrical or mechanical failures down the road.
One technology that’s mitigating these issues is acoustic micro imaging (AMI). AMI is a high-frequency ultrasound technology, and it’s being used by the industry as an inspection method.
At the core of AMI technology is a transducer, or a device that turns energy from one form to another. It starts with a pulse of electrical energy, then converts it to mechanical energy, or a high-frequency ultrasound wave. Because ultrasound doesn’t travel through air, this allows inspectors to obtain clear images of gaps and delaminations in the device that could otherwise be difficult to see.
However, the transducers used for AMI are not all the same. Each transducer handles a specific frequency, and they’re chosen based on the sample that needs to be inspected. articles.title: Why does your body store fat in your butt?
articles.summary:
Curious Kids is a series for children of all ages. If you have a question you’d like an expert to answer, send it to CuriousKidsUS@theconversation.com.
Why does your body store fat in your butt? - Ellen, age 8, Cambridge, Massachusetts
Have you ever wondered why some parts of your body are firm, like your elbows, while other areas, like your butt, are squishier?
The difference is due to what scientists call fat distribution, and researchers are still trying to understand why bodies store fat in some places but not in others.
All animals have fat in their bodies, even insects. Bears even put on up to 400 pounds (180 kilograms) of additional body fat, the equivalent of 544 large cheese pizzas, to survive hibernation.
Fat is an important and constantly changing part of all bodies, including those of humans and our evolutionary ancestors.
What is fat?
Fat, also called adipose tissue, is one kind of connective tissue that helps hold your body together.
For a long time, scientists thought that adipose tissue was mainly a storage place for the extra energy your body doesn’t use from the food you eat. While fat is a great source of stored energy, it also has many other functions. There are even different kinds of fat.

articles.title: How does a compass work?
articles.summary:
If you’re like me, when you pick up a compass you can’t help but spin it this way and that, to see if you can trick it. It’s hard to resist experimenting with a spooky force we can’t see or feel ourselves. Yet it always turns the compass needle back towards north.
Even in today’s high-tech world, compasses are useful navigation tools. A compass works without power, unlike GPS, and in any weather and lighting conditions, as opposed to navigation using the Sun, stars or landmarks. If you know which way north is, you can determine any direction.
Like all cool phenomena, the explanation of how a compass works is not magic – it’s physics. And people have been making use of this particular aspect of physics for more than 2,000 years.
A lodestone spoon
The earliest versions of the compass were developed in ancient China. They were spoon-shaped and made of lodestones, pieces of the naturally magnetic mineral magnetite.
When allowed to rotate freely, the spoon handle would align itself with a particular direction (north–south). This was used to organise and harmonise environments, as part of a practice you might know as feng shui.
At the time, it was known that some materials were naturally magnetic – able to attract one another. However, it wasn’t clear exactly what was causing a compass to align itself north–south until 1600, when English physicist William Gilbert deduced that Earth itself acted as a giant magnet.

Serena Williams and longtime business partner Beth Ferreira announced Monday the launch of an early-stage firm called Starfire Ventures.
The firm is seeking to raise $200 million in capital to back AI-native companies that are “solving critical, underserved problems for individuals across the experience economy,” including in areas such as fintech and health and wellness, the fund said in a press release announcing its launch.
This fund is separate from Serena Ventures, which Williams founded in 2022. Serena Ventures backed more than 100 companies and raised over $100 million in capital. This new firm, Starfire, is a continuation of that business partnership, with Williams saying in the press release that it was “designed to live beyond” them and that the goal remains to broaden “access to capital” and create “opportunities for more people to participate in the ownership and growth of transformative businesses.”

Bringing Black Holes Into Focus
Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process.
With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit, black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes.
By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time.
The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull.

articles.title: Uber Data Breach Impacts 150,000 People
articles.summary:
Uber is notifying roughly 150,000 drivers that their personal information was stolen in a data breach involving a third-party services provider.
The company learned of the incident on October 9 and immediately severed its data connections with the provider and launched an investigation.
On October 13, the investigation determined that the hackers used compromised service provider credentials on October 7 to access data Uber had shared with the provider.
According to Uber, the hackers accessed images of driver’s licenses and personal information such as names, addresses, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers, and government-issued ID numbers.

Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.

Qué ocurre con el aire que atraviesa un parque eólico
Los aerogeneradores aprovechan la energía del viento. Como consecuencia, crean estelas. Estas estelas están a sotavento (dirección de propagación del viento). En ellas se reduce la velocidad y aumenta la turbulencia. El alcance de estas estelas depende de las condiciones atmosféricas y de cómo se dispongan las máquinas.
Astrid Lampert y colaboradores han publicado un trabajo en agosto de 2026 en la revista Wind Energy Science donde analizan medidas en parques marinos de la bahía alemana. La respuesta a estas preguntas solo las conocen las propias empresas que operan los centros de datos. No hay información pública y transparente al respecto. articles.title: Reducing High-Bandwidth Flash Latency In GPU Systems (Georgia Tech, Nvidia, Stanford)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Georgia Tech, NVIDIA Research, and Stanford University published “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.”
Abstract Excerpt
“Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20μs, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering.
We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines …

Benefitting from mistakes

O problema não é a inteligência artificial por si só. O ponto de conflito está no uso de ferramentas que “caçam bugs” no Linux com auxílio da IA e, principalmente, nos códigos gerados por elas. Em linhas gerais, esses mecanismos têm produzido um volume muito grande de relatórios de falhas e sugestões de patches, a ponto de os desenvolvedores terem dificuldade para lidar com tudo isso.
Talvez a pior parte seja o fato de boa parte desses relatórios ou patches estarem relacionados a bugs com baixa de prioridade, que já estavam na fila de correção ou até que foram corrigidos recentemente.
Mas, sim, a IA também tem conseguido apontar problemas ou pontos de ajustes legítimos, mas em um ritmo com o qual os desenvolvedores do Linux não estavam habituados. Ao que tudo indica, foi isso que fez Stoakes reduzir a sua participação no projeto.

articles.title: Hackers Probe Newly Disclosed Flaws in Copeland Refrigeration Controllers
articles.summary:
Exploitation attempts against a vulnerability in Copeland’s XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers began less than two hours after the issue was made public last week, according to VulnCheck.
The security firm disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in XWEB EVO, a Dixell supervisory system now sold under the Copeland name. VulnCheck’s Valentin Lobstein said each flaw was shown to yield root privileges on test systems.
The product drew the researcher’s attention after the October 11-12 attack that triggered defrost cycles at roughly 700 French supermarkets. CERT-FR named Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers among the compromised products, and France has blamed Iran for the campaign.
Nine of the flaws disclosed by VulnCheck only affect firmware builds that predate a 2021 rewrite. They include unauthenticated command execution, a hardcoded administrator password, and command injection via the login page.
The other five vulnerabilities also impact the latest firmware. Four of them involve predictable credentials: the administrator’s daily password is generated from the device’s MAC address and the current date, and the MAC address is exposed to unauthenticated users.
An attacker can calculate the password offline, enable SSH, and log in as root, since the root password is built from the same daily code. The fifth flaw is a command injection issue that requires authentication.
These five issues will not be fixed. Copeland ended software support for the XWEB EVO family on March 16, 2026, and has …

What just happened? Drone users who complain that rules related to UAVs are too tough should be thankful they don't live in Beijing. A law came into effect in the Chinese capital yesterday that makes owning and storing the devices illegal, meaning you can't even keep a drone that you never fly.
While many Chinese cities have no-fly zones in sensitive areas for civilian drones, Beijing is the only one to ban ownership.
The restrictions cover the entire municipality, including its rural areas, spanning around 16,400 square kilometers (6,332 square miles), around half the size of Belgium. Bringing drones or their components into Beijing is also forbidden, so leaving one packed away in your luggage won't get you around the rules.
Authorities announced the extreme measure in September, claiming it was a requirement to keep the city secure. Beijing had already banned drone sales in May, but registered owners were initially allowed to keep their devices if they registered them with authorities, a luxury that has now disappeared.
In June, a small plane crashed into Beijing's tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 people. It raised concerns about airspace safety and led to the current drone restrictions.
There are a handful of exemptions that allow drones to be owned and used, including activities involving law enforcement, counterterrorism, emergency relief, agriculture, and scientific research.

Cinq failles critiques dans la mémoire de Chrome
Parmi les 83 brèches, cinq ont été jugées « critiques », le niveau de gravité le plus élevé, par les ingénieurs de Google. Les 78 autres sont de sévérité « élevée ». Cette fois, Google n’a pas découvert de tentative d’exploitation des failles. Les cinq failles critiques concernent la gestion de la mémoire. Concrètement, Chrome libère une zone de la mémoire, mais continue ensuite de s’en servir. Un pirate peut alors glisser des données malveillantes dans cet espace. Les chercheurs de Malwarebytes soulignent que ce problème de mémoire peut provoquer des « plantages, des corruptions de données et des fuites d’informations ».
L’une des failles de sévérité a déjà retenu l’attention des cybercriminels. articles.title: Georgina Rodríguez: “Dejé el currículum en Inditex y empecé en Massimo Dutti, pero paseaba a veces por la Milla de Oro y me encantaba ver los escaparates. Cuando entraba a una boutique de lujo, para mí era como entrar en un museo”

En una entrevista, Georgina Rodríguez explicaba que había dejado el currículum en Inditex y había empezado en Massimo Dutti. Pero también paseaba por la Milla de Oro. Le gustaba mirar cómo eran los escaparates.
Así conseguía ir acercándose a las tiendas que realmente le interesaban. Cuando entraba en alguna boutique de lujo, se sentía como en un museo. Antes de llegar a Gucci, trabajó en un hotel y también estuvo en Inglaterra cuidando niños.
Vivía con su madre y su hermana antes de irse a Madrid. Según contaba, estuvieron muy unidas. Nunca les faltó lo básico. Hubo momentos mejores y peores. En algunos días comían mejor que en otros, e incluso hubo días en los que no había agua caliente.
Cuando tenía 18 años le ofrecieron un trabajo en un hotel de un pueblo cerca de Barbastro (a dos horas y media de Jaca). Entonces, su madre le dejó 100 euros para que pudiera irse del pueblo. Empezó a tener sueldo propio. Pagaba un alquiler y vivía de forma independiente.

Compromised passwords and gaps in multi-factor authentication (MFA) remain common ways attackers gain access to sensitive systems. For law enforcement agencies handling criminal justice information (CJI), protecting against these threats is also a matter of CJIS compliance.
The FBI's latest CJIS Security Policy sets clear requirements for password management and MFA. these are Priority 1 (P1) controls, so must be implemented immediately to comply. But this can be challenging, particularly across the complex IT environments that are common in law enforcement.
This guide contains practical tips to help agencies meet the latest requirements, strengthen their defenses against credential-based attacks, and make ongoing compliance easier to manage.
1. Enforce Stronger Minimum Password Lengths
CJIS requires user-selected passwords to be at least eight characters long, or six characters if generated by a credential service provider or verifier using an approved random number generator. However, we recommend going beyond these minimums and encouraging passphrases of at least 15 characters.
Longer passwords are generally harder to crack, and passphrases can be easier to remember than shorter passwords with complex combinations of symbols and numbers.
CJIS doesn't require traditional complexity rules, so focus on length and strength rather than arbitrary character requirements.

This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria now has rules that officially recognise stablecoins as payment and settlement instruments, giving issuers a framework to distribute tokens backed by fiat currencies. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) divides these tokens into two: naira-referenced and foreign currency-referenced stablecoins.
Stablecoins are digital currencies designed to maintain the value of currencies such as the naira or US dollar. Companies issuing them must hold enough money and other assets to back the tokens in circulation—which they create.
Under the new rules, foreign currency-backed issuers must hold up to ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) in minimum capital, while naira-backed issuers must hold ₦10 billion ($7.44 million). But the more consequential requirements concern what happens to customers’ money after they buy stablecoins.
Stablecoin holders cannot earn interest on their tokens, even though issuers can invest the money backing those tokens in interest-bearing assets. Cryptocurrency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers (VASPs) distributing regulated stablecoins cannot offer yield on behalf of issuers either.

It was amid the stillness of the Covid-19 lockdowns that Conrad Young, founder and CEO of Chirrup.ai, realized that birdsong would make an excellent proxy for biodiversity. Birds have always acted as sentinels for changes in the environment, and as he told EE Times, “Birdsong is a pretty powerful and visceral way of understanding what’s going on in the environment but is also scientifically valid and benchmarkable.”
In March 2022, as the pandemic ended, Young launched Chirrup.ai to monitor birdsong and track farmland diversity. The first task was to deploy acoustic sensors and establish a baseline of bird activity that could provide a reference point against future recordings and reveal whether biodiversity was improving, declining, or remaining stable over time. Earlier trials used audiomoths—low-cost, acoustic loggers that record birdsong—but Chirrup.ai has now developed smart acoustic sensors.
The sensor pairs a MEMS analog microphone with a 24-bit digital audio codec, a 240-MHz processor with Bluetooth, and a high-speed 4G LTE modem. A multi-constellation GNSS receiver supporting GPS, GLONASS, and Galileo provides geolocation and timestamping for the acoustic data. The device is powered by a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery.

In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. articles.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a high-severity vulnerability in the open source Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server UnrealIRCd one day after public disclosure.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS score: 8.6), the flaw is described as an improper neutralization of delimiters and allows attackers to execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges.
The issue exists because the labeled-response module “does not escape the IRCv3 ‘label’ message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority,” according to a NIST advisory.
Patches for CVE-2026-114713 and eight other bugs were released on November 7 in UnrealIRCd version 6.2.7.1. A hot patch was also rolled out.
According to UnrealIRCd project leader, developer, and maintainer Bram Matthys, this is the most severe security defect discovered in UnrealIRCd.
“Any ordinary user can KILL, GLINE, and do many more bad things. This is the most critical issue found in UnrealIRCd in the past 15 years,” Matthys said.
Matthys has provided instructions on how to update to UnrealIRCd 6.2.7.1 or apply the hot patch and warned that UnrealIRCd 5 and previous releases have reached End of Life (EoL) and won’t receive a fix.
“It is likely that several bugs that are fixed in 6.2.7.1 go all the way back to 3.2.x,” Matthys said.

Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.
“Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”
In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics.
Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale
Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity.
In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute.

articles.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing
Enterprise teams are building multi-agent systems, and when early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model. Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, and many teams taking it on haven’t yet built distributed systems instincts.
The numbers are consistent across sources: ~88% of AI pilots never reach production. Stanford HAI demonstrated that two models can perform worse collaborating than either alone when coordination overhead exceeds the benefit. The pattern is clear: teams are adding complexity faster than they build understanding. Ten steps that are each 95 percent reliable deliver only 59.9 percent end-to-end reliability, and 20 steps deliver 35.8 percent. This illustrative model assumes a strictly sequential chain with no retries, but the direction holds: each dependent handoff multiplies risk.
In this post, you learn how to decide whether a use case needs multiple agents, choose a coordination pattern, and spot costly anti-patterns early. You also see how takt time, safety boundaries, edge data, and shift cycles shape the architecture.
Multi-agent coordination patterns
Coordination patterns fall into two tiers, based on who controls the flow. In Tier 1, you define the path.
In Tier 2, the model chooses the path at runtime. That flexibility handles work whose steps you can’t define in advance, at a higher cost in tokens, latency…

Developer creates a 100% valid ZIP file that doubles as a BIOS-bootable operating system — hiding BIOS boot flags inside uncompressed files and turning file headers into CPU instructions
The original definition of "hacking" was making hardware and software do something it wasn't supposed to.
Hacking stories these days mostly involve someone using an army of AI agents to find vulnerabilities in networks and software that were carefully hidden in plain sight. Today, for a change, we have a story about hacking in its original meaning — twisting computing artifacts into purposes not in their design spec. David Oberhollenzer, aka Goliath, a greybeard in spirit if not in shade, crafted a 100% valid ZIP file that's simultaneously an archive, BIOS-bootable, and a Multiboot-compatible OS image.
You can unpack the ZIP file just like any other, boot it using Linux's GRUB, QEMU, or any other Multiboot-compatible loader (even if imaged to different media), or alternatively, perform the finest party trick: image-write it to a floppy and boot from it directly from BIOS on any compatible PC, without modification.

The first thing you need to know is that unlike most file types, the metadata (in this case, file directory) of a ZIP is actually at the end of the archive. Telegram CEO Pavel Durov promoted the widgets feature on X on November 10, saying that any message on the platform can now become an app.

articles.title: Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw
articles.summary:
A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild.
The flaw comes from the way OpenSSH checks passwords when musl handles the underlying crypt() call. On an affected system, a password longer than 256 bytes causes musl to return an error value. That value is an asterisk, the same character Linux uses in /etc/shadow to mark an account as having no password. OpenSSH then treats the returned asterisk as a match and permits the login.
The conditions to exploit the vulnerability are however quite narrow. The server must run OpenSSH before version 10.6p2, be built against the musl library rather than glibc, and operate without PAM. It must also have at least one account with a SHA-256 or SHA-512 password hash and another account marked with an asterisk in its shadow entry. When those conditions are met, any password between 257 and 1,024 characters can authenticate against the passwordless account.
Alpine Linux is the most prominent distribution affected, as it uses musl and its default OpenSSH configuration does not enable PAM. Other musl-based environments, including OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto, may also be affected where the same configuration applies. Systems using glibc, PAM, …

articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
While we’re used to predictable technology, AI challenges that assumption. Therefore, the goal must be bounded, observable, and controllable AI.
Provided byUL Solutions
In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors.
For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses.
AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built.
We will not make AI trustworthy by predicting what it will do. We will do it by fencing it in with hard limits that are enforced outside its reach. In OpenAI’s case, the safeguards sat inside a system the agents could edit. But a fence the agents can …

According to the team’s benchmarks, 7.0 is about 2x faster at the median and 5x smaller than 6.7, with some operations, such as brush creation, up to 38x faster. articles.title: Intel sued by shareholders who claim it hid PC sales slump before 29% stock crash
articles.summary:
What just happened? It's not just Nvidia being sued by its shareholders over claims it withheld important information. Intel is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit over allegations it hid the severity of the decline in PC sales, which the plaintiffs say caused the company's stock to crash almost 29% in one day.
The complaint, filed in federal court in San Jose on November 13, names Intel, CEO Lip-Bu Tan, and CFO David Zinsner as defendants. Michigan's City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System is leading the case, seeking unspecified damages.
Shareholders allege Intel took too long to disclose how weakening PC sales and a buildup of unsold inventory would hurt revenue. They argue those problems outweighed the benefits Team Blue was receiving from data center construction and the AI boom.
The suit specifically accuses Intel of making "materially false and/or misleading" statements that suggested demand was improving. Investors say October's results undermined those assurances, revealing the extent of the PC slowdown after they had bought shares at allegedly inflated prices. The complaint covers purchases between July 23 and October 29.
Despite third-quarter earnings beating expectations and data center revenue jumping almost 80%, Intel's outlook disappointed investors. On October 29, the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below Wall Street's roughly $17 billion estimate, and warned of a prolonged PC slowdown. Hackers who breached the cloud environment of network and email security company Barracuda earlier this month used a stolen cloud access key and the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework.
The company says the attacker accessed approximately 10 of its cloud accounts over a 44-hour period between November 1 and 2.
The attacker's presence was discovered on November 4, and Barracuda's investigation determined that the open-source AI pentesting framework ARTEX was used for this "machine-speed intrusion."
The company explains that the attacker leveraged a cloud access key provided to a third-party vendor for the duration of a previous project.
"We did not retire the key when the vendor — a company working in AI — finished that work. That is on us," Barracuda says.
The security company believes the attacker stole the key from the unnamed third-party AI vendor in October. It confirmed that the key was stored in a configuration file in the vendor's GitHub repository.
The attacker used credentials they found in one system to move through Barracuda’s data analytics environment, source-code repositories, and Kubernetes clusters.
Based on the attacker's commands targeting cryptocurrency-related secrets, including private keys, Ethereum keystore files, and seed phrases, Barracuda believes the attack was financially motivated.

articles.title: Beyond payments: Where venture capital will flow across Indian fintech over the next 24 months
articles.summary:
Beyond payments: Where venture capital will flow across Indian fintech over the next 24 months
India's fintech decade was built on distribution. The next one will be built on infrastructure, advice and intelligence—and capital is already repricing accordingly.
India spent the last ten years solving for reach. UPI, Aadhaar-based onboarding, and the Jan Dhan push put a payment instrument in almost every adult hand, and a generation of companies was built on that distribution. That problem is now largely solved. The harder question—how to serve those hundreds of millions of customers profitably, with products that measurably improve their financial lives—is where the next cycle of venture capital will go.
The funding data already reflects the shift. Indian fintech attracted $3.5 billion across 216 disclosed deals in 2024, and $2.9 billion across 156 deals in 2025 roughly 10% less capital across 27% fewer transactions, according to Fintech Global. This fits fewer, larger cheques into a narrower set of theses. Yet fintech remained the largest sector by funding in 2025 at 22% of all Indian startup capital, and close to 26% in the first half of 2026. Capital is not leaving the sector; it is becoming far more selective about where to park itself.
Three themes stand out as most likely to absorb that capital over the next 24 months.
Financial infrastructure: Rebuilding the core

South African value-based care startup Alignd has raised an undisclosed amount of funding from Knife Capital to fund its expansion beyond palliative care into maternity and kidney care.
Founded in 2018, Alignd designs value-based care programmes that align the interests of patients, healthcare providers and medical schemes. Instead of paying for volume, its model ties payment to the outcomes that matter to patients. It coordinates care across clinical teams and, where appropriate, brings care into the home.
The startup started with palliative care. Medical schemes there have traditionally covered costly in-hospital end-of-life care but not home-based support. Alignd has built a network of more than 500 providers delivering home-based, person-centred care, working with seven medical schemes. Its palliative programme reaches more than 3.3 million lives.
It has also launched two newer programmes – a maternity programme that links parents, providers and schemes in a coordinated ecosystem, with support tailored to each family; and a kidney care programme, which coordinates care for patients with chronic kidney disease, helping them preserve kidney function for as long as possible while helping schemes manage long-term costs.
To scale those programmes, Aligned has raised an undisclosed amount of funding from Knife Capital, via Knife Fund III.

Voyager 1 ist bald einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt: So läuft die Kommunikation mit der Nasa-Sonde
Seit 49 Jahren schwebt die Raumsonde Voyager 1 durchs Weltall. Trotz ihrer alten Tage ist die Sonde noch teilweise funktionsfähig. Und schon bald wird sie einen Meilenstein erreichen, den zuvor noch kein anderes menschengemachtes Objekt im Weltall erreichen konnte.
Voyager 1 erreicht historische Lichttag-Distanz
Die Raumsonde wird als erstes einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt sein. Dies entspricht etwa 25,9 Milliarden Kilometern. Wie das Wort „Lichttag“ schon sagt: Das Licht, das von einem Objekt in dieser Distanz ausgestrahlt wird, benötigt 24 Stunden, um die Erde zu erreichen. Die Nasa hat den Moment, an dem Voyager 1 einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt sein wird, schon exakt berechnet. Demnach ist es am 18. November um 5:16 Uhr US-Ostküstenzeit so weit. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt wird die Distanz der Sonde zur Erde exakt 25.902.068.356 Kilometer betragen.
Ein Radiosignal, das die Kontrollstation auf der Erde in Richtung Voyager abschickt, ist dann ebenfalls einen ganzen Tag unterwegs. Das sorgt für massive Delays in der Kommunikation. „Wenn man ‚Voyager ‚Hallo‘ sagen will, schickt man seine Nachricht ab, geht nach Hause und wartet zwei Tage, bis man endlich eine Antwort bekommt“, sagte Suzanne Dodd vom Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) der Nasa in der Mitteilung.

The FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S. and globally. The campaigns include a widespread hack of customers of American IT company ConnectWise and across South Korea’s financial industry.
In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory, the FBI says hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks.
Artex is one of several open source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that make it far more difficult for human defenders to keep up.
In some cases, Artex-linked attacks can move from targeting a system to active compromise “in under three hours.”

In August, Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air delivery drone program to “nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.” Combined with similar uncrewed aerial delivery programs from DoorDash and Zipline (in partnership with Uber and Walmart), the expansion suggests that flying robots dropping their payloads onto suburban lawns will soon be commonplace.
For many people, delivery drones will be little more than a novelty, occasionally good for a laugh when one does something ridiculous. For others, though, their growing use could be a nightmare. As the instant delivery industry clears the last FAA hurdles to rapid deliveries beyond an operator’s line of sight, an increasing number of people worldwide are living with post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety-related disorders triggered by drones.
The use of all manner of weaponized drones in the ongoing war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has already produced an epidemic of what some mental health professionals have dubbed “dronophobia.” And while relatively few US troops have been targeted by drones flown by Iran, ISIS, and Iran-backed militias throughout the Middle East, even those who have not directly been attacked may experience anxiety simply because of the ample video footage of attacks circulating in news and social media.

Built by YHWH Vision Ventures Technologies Ltd., which was formally incorporated in 2025, Tratum traces its origins to Nigeria’s 2023 cash scarcity crisis, when millions of people had money in their bank accounts but struggled to access or use it.
“If money is increasingly digital, why should access to that money completely depend on a functioning network, a smartphone, a remote server or a particular digital channel at the exact moment someone needs to transact?” said Segun Ademigoke, the startup’s founder and CEO.
At the heart of the ecosystem is the Tratum Node, a secure physical financial endpoint that combines secure hardware, cryptographic device identity, local transaction state and communication capabilities. Under rules set by the institution, a Node can carry out approved transactions locally, record them cryptographically, and then synchronise and reconcile with the bank’s systems once connectivity returns.
“We are not trying to become the bank, replace the central bank or compete with consumer-facing financial institutions. We are building technology that those institutions can use to extend what they already do,” Ademigoke said.

Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty
Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release.
Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.
He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023 because of his autism, but in January, Kurtaj was deemed fit for trial and moved to prison, the BBC reports.

articles.title: Google Project Zero Sets Course for 30-Day Disclosure Deadline
articles.summary:
In the context of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation, Google Project Zero is significantly shrinking bug disclosure windows.
So far, Project Zero’s policy has been a well-known one: vendors were given 90 days to patch vulnerabilities before public disclosure and granted a 30-day grace period for patch roll-out.
Starting November 13, that grace period is no longer in the books, Project Zero security engineer Natalie Silvanovich announced.
Under the new ‘Full X’ policy, Project Zero will publish vulnerability details 90 days after reporting them to the vendor, regardless of whether, or when, a fix is released.
Beginning February 2, 2027, Project Zero will disclose vulnerabilities publicly after 60 days, and the disclosure window will shrink to 30 days on January 3, 2028.
Furthermore, Project Zero is removing most ‘special cases’ from its disclosure policy, except for security defects actively exploited in the wild (which have a 7-day disclosure window, per Google’s policy) and flaws already made public by others.
If a vendor requests it, Project Zero may publish details on a security hole ahead of the deadline, Silvanovich says.
However, serious vulnerabilities may be granted exceptions. Project Zero has done it on rare occasions, such as Spectre and Meltdown, and that will not change.
According to Silvanovich, the phased transition to shorter disclosure windows addresses concerns that users may be exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities, that vendors may rush to…

AWS has launched Nitro Sandboxes, which run an opted-in Kubernetes pod, ECS task, or EC2 workload inside its own lightweight virtual machine with a separate guest kernel, carved out of a running EC2 instance by the Nitro hypervisor. On Amazon EKS, the whole change is one pod field: runtimeClassName: isolated-sandbox or confidential-sandbox.
The feature is available in all commercial regions at no additional charge, and AWS positions it for workloads where the tenant or the code cannot be trusted, with coding agents named first. In an AWS blog post, Carlos Santana and Trishi Mehta write:
Each pod gets its own operating system, completely separate from the host and from every neighbor.
According to the EKS documentation, a containerd-shim-nitro-sandbox-v2 process on the parent instance launches a Firecracker microVM as a first-level guest with hardware-assisted virtualization, after which an agent inside the VM runs the pod’s containers through its own containerd and the two sides communicate over virtio and vsock. The result is a sandbox that shares neither kernel nor memory mappings with the parent instance or any other sandbox, while the containers themselves start unchanged. How the nodes get there depends on the cluster type: on EKS Auto Mode the two RuntimeClasses ship with every cluster and sandbox-capable nodes are provisioned on demand, whereas on standard EKS a team builds a sandbox-enabled AMI for its node groups or Karpenter.

articles.title: Google Project Zero cuts bug disclosures to 30 days amid AI threats
articles.summary:
Google Project Zero will replace its “90+30” disclosure policy with shorter, fixed deadlines in response to AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation.
The transition is gradual and began on November 13, when the 30-day extension was removed from the vulnerability disclosure timeline.
On February 2, 2027, the deadline will be further reduced to 60 days, and on January 3, 2028, it will shrink to just 30 days.
Once the deadline expires, Project Zero will publish vulnerability details even if a fix is not available.
Project Zero is Google’s vulnerability research team, focused on the discovery of serious security flaws in widely used software and hardware.
Some of its notable recent findings include a .NET Framework zero-day, flaws in Chrome’s JavaScript engine and graphics components, and a Qualcomm chipset zero-day linked to NoviSpy spyware attacks.
When the team finds a flaw, it reports it privately to the vendor and typically publishes the technical details after a set period, giving time for developing security updates and patches, as well as a margin for most users to apply them.
Project Zero says AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and made it easier for attackers to reverse-engineer fixes as soon as patches ship and develop working exploits.
This policy change puts greater pressure on vendors to investigate reports, develop fixes, and ship them faster to customers.

articles.title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests Without Jank
articles.summary:
GitHub engineering has published a detailed account of how it rebuilt the diff surface in the GitHub Copilot app to open a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and more than 400 inline review comments without turning the review into a waiting exercise.
The post, by Principal Design Engineer Alberto Gimeno, lands at a moment when AI coding agents are producing far more pull requests than reviewers can digest, and the bottleneck has moved from writing code to reading it.
At the heart of the rebuild is a decision to stop pretending a pull request is a single uniform list. Code rows have a known height at a known font size, so their geometry can be computed up front and never rebuilt. Comments do not. A markdown body wraps differently at different widths, <details> sections can be toggled in place, reply composers grow as a user types, and images change height when they load. Rather than force one variable-height virtualizer to absorb both, the team split the document into two independent domains:
total height = deterministic code height
 + Σ dynamic block effective heights
 + scroll padding
Dynamic blocks are keyed by identity (file, line, side) rather than pixel position, with a fingerprint tracking content, open state and measurement width. A single idle-gated measurement pass reads mounted blocks in one batch, scoped to roughly 2,400 pixels around the viewport, and corrections are anchored to whatever the reader is looking at so the surface never fights…

Soon after, the links between pilots and controllers and the radar feeds that track aircraft started failing.
The result was more than 3,500 flights held for about five hours, leaving tens of thousands of travelers stranded.
The volume of traffic was far beyond anything the network normally handles. "We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds," Rebecca Guy, the FAA's technology chief, said on Saturday at a press conference.
El Dorado was one of those two places. The other was a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, which had been upgraded several weeks earlier and showed a second problem that officials have not described. Engineers took both sites offline, but by then each had been hitting the network hundreds of times per second. That was enough to knock out other parts of the air traffic communications system, and the delays and cancellations carried into the weekend.

articles.title: La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal lo confirma: si un vecino no paga, los propietarios podrían apelar al artículo 21
articles.summary:
Cuando un vecino de tu edificio deja de pagar sus cuotas, la comunidad de propietarios tiene un camino marcado en el artículo 21 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal. Esta ley permite que la comunidad pueda reclamar la deuda por vía judicial e incluso llegar al embargo.
Lo que dice el artículo 21. El precepto regula el impago de los gastos comunes, las medidas que puede pactar la comunidad, la reclamación judicial y la mediación o el arbitraje, y buena parte de ese contenido se incorporó con la Ley 10/2022. Y es que fue esa reforma la que permitió a la junta aprobar medidas disuasorias contra los morosos, siempre que no sean abusivas ni afecten a la habitabilidad.
La obligación de pagar está en el artículo 9.1.e de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, y para reclamar lo que se debe la comunidad puede tirar del proceso monitorio especial, sin que el artículo 21 fije un importe máximo.
Sin voto mientras haya deuda. ¿Y qué pasa en las juntas? Pues que, según el artículo 15.2, quien no esté al corriente de sus deudas al empezar la reunión puede participar en las deliberaciones, pero no votar, salvo que las haya impugnado judicialmente o haya consignado lo que debe. Además, el artículo 16.2 obliga a que la convocatoria incluya la relación de propietarios que no están al corriente de pago.
Vamos, que dentro de la comunidad sí puede saberse quién debe, aunque con cuidado. También se puede crear una lista de deudores en el tablón de anuncios de la comunidad, aunque la Agencia Española de Pro…

articles.title: Usable Security at Luxury Hotels - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Usable Security at Luxury Hotels
Interesting case study from luxury hotels. Attackers used a fake booking request to gain access to a reservations inbox, where they copied genuine refund requests and got fraudulent ones approved.
This is a good illustration why “just don’t click on links” is bad advice. It can’t work when answering strangers’ emails is the job. Even worse, in this case the guest-first culture punishes hesitation. More interesting, the case study shows that splitting security between owner, operator, and brand leaves nobody accountable. And this is exactly the setting where blaming staff becomes the convenient answer.
TimH • November 16, 2026 7:22 AM
TFA: “We suspect a colleague opened the email and clicked the link, unknowingly giving the attackers access to the reservations shared inbox.”
So there was no front-end layer checking inbox content for such dubiosities? Or limiting access to specific computer MACs, or intranet IP ranges.
The ball is in the IT org’s court for not setting this up.
Same with IT who can’t set a limit of 5 CCs on emails to stop an email blast CCing every customer.

The demo's 3D space and textures are all procedurally generated, meaning they're the result of mathematical equations rather than prebuilt 3D meshes, and all calculated on load. Using actual meshes and images for textures would otherwise take up a significant amount of space.
Building structures procedurally is difficult and has limitations, but it's exceedingly effective when used properly. Some games employ this technique for repeated elements like trees and grass.
Likewise, all the visual effects and even some texturing are done with shaders, which are small programs that change how a mesh or texture appears — for example, to make parts of an object shiny. articles.title: Old Bitly links hijacked in X posts from Trump, McDonald's, Burger King, and others

In context: Back when tweets were capped at 140 characters, brands and politicians ran most of their links through Bitly to shrink them down. That's why years of old posts on X are still full of tiny bit.ly addresses. Click one, and the service quietly forwards you to the full web page sitting behind it. Most people wouldn't think twice before doing that. Over the weekend, pranksters managed to take over some of those old links in posts from Donald Trump, McDonald's and Burger King.
CNN found that Trump's account was hit the hardest. At least a dozen of his posts now carry swapped links, including a 2013 complaint about wind turbines. Open it today, and you'll land on a Google site called "fortnite baby," complete with a photo of an infant.
Over at Burger King, a 2011 post meant to help people find nearby restaurants now leads to Wikipedia's list of Nazi concentration camps. McDonald's didn't escape either – one of its 2011 posts now opens a page about the September 11 attacks.
Bill Gates, former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau and Mike Pence all had old posts tampered with as well. Weirdly, the FBI's 2012 post about its "Ghost Clicks" case now just shows a photo of a seal.
In theory, none of this should be possible. Bitly's own help pages say the code at the end of a short link can never be reused, even after the account that created it gets deleted.

Teams point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at it with environment variables such as AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, leaving application code unchanged. On Linux it installs as an RPM or Debian package for x86_64 or aarch64; on macOS and Windows, AWS documents a short Dockerfile and does not publish a prebuilt image. Rust tests can use an embedded mode that runs the emulator inside the test process and wires its HTTP client into the AWS SDK for Rust. An aws-emulator skill can start the emulator for coding agents and check a project against published fidelity tests. Written in Rust, it is generated from more than 400 Smithy API models AWS publishes for the SDKs, according to Swaminathan Sivasubramanian.
AWS says agents wrote and tested the code. Matthew Goldberg, a senior principal engineer at AWS, describes three teams: one writes fidelity tests from the public API models and verifies them against real AWS, one replays those tests and files issues, and one implements each fix. The company confirmed to BleepingComputer that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to inject malicious JavaScript into customer projects, causing websites using the platform to load malware.

We have also ended active sessions, revoked tokens, and reset access for affected user accounts. Finally, we have blocked any code from being delivered in Cloudflare.

Xpressbees has raised Rs 100 crore through secured, unlisted NCDs, at a 13.5% coupon over 36 months, to fund its working capital needs.

The company's board approved the allotment on October 22, 2026. It issued 2,000 NCDs of Rs 5 lakh each through a private placement. BlackSoil Capital took 1,200 of them for Rs 60 crore, and BlackSoil India Credit Fund II took the remaining 800 for Rs 40 crore.
The debt carries an interest of 13.5% a year, paid monthly. It runs for 36 months, and the principal will be repaid in equal instalments. The documents also mention a second tranche, which suggests the money may come in more than one go.
The NCDs are backed by a claim on the company's assets, including cash flows, inventory and receivables, and excludes intellectual property. The promoters and directors are not putting in any money.
Xpressbees can repay early after 12 months. It will pay a 2% premium if it does so between months 13 and 17, and 1% between months 18 and 23. After 24 months, there is no premium.

Après 4 ans d’enquête, le parquet de Paris a décidé de poursuivre l’entreprise. Une première audience de fixation aura lieu le 25 février 2027, avant des plaidoiries qui se tiendront sur plusieurs jours en juin 2027.
Le procès ne portera pas sur un ralentissement volontaire des iPhone ou sur une durée de vie limitée (d’autres accusations de HOP). Le parquet s’appuie sur un délit plus précis : l’entrave à la réparation et au reconditionnement, inscrite à l’article L441-3 du Code de la consommation depuis 2021. C’est la première fois qu’un procureur s’en sert pour engager des poursuites.
Ce que la justice reproche à Apple
Selon le dossier de presse de HOP, diffusé le 17 novembre 2026, 24 modèles d’iPhone sont visés sur une période qui court du 17 novembre 2021 au 23 juillet 2024. La loi interdit aux fabricants les techniques, y compris logicielles, qui visent à rendre impossible une réparation hors de leurs circuits agréés ou à limiter les fonctionnalités d’un appareil réparé ailleurs. Le mot « viser » compte : le tribunal devra établir une intention, pas seulement constater une contrainte.

U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he does not believe the country’s national security was put at risk as a result of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump went on to contradict previous findings from U.S. officials by doubting that Huang’s paramour, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy.

Last year, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw the production of an internal memo, circulated among top policymakers, which warned that Alice Huang was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. But Trump has maintained that he was not aware of these claims.

Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Ce lundi 16 novembre, Apple a détaillé dans une note aux développeurs comment la deuxième bêta de macOS 27.3 découpe ces droits.
Apple avait prévenu le 2 octobre, dans un premier message aux développeurs. La marque y reprochait à certains d’utiliser l’accès complet au disque d’une façon qui expose fichiers, mails, messages et historique de navigation sans que l’utilisateur le comprenne vraiment. Mail oui, Messages non

43-year-old Roman Khlynovskiy was an alleged member of the "8-Digits Team" ransomware group, known for its affiliation with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations.
Together with his accomplices, Khlynovskiy is believed to have extorted victims in at least six US states (including hospitals and schools) after breaching their networks and stealing sensitive data.
After exfiltrating data from victims' compromised systems, they pressured them to pay the ransoms by threatening to release the stolen files online.
"The conspirators boasted that they possessed over 50 terabytes of data consisting of more than 70 million confidential health records," the Department of Justice said.
"The conspirators also threatened to publicize this highly sensitive medical information to increase pressure on victims to pay ransom demands. The coconspirators' actions resulted in over $500 million in ransom demands."
Khlynovskiy faces up to 27 years in prison if convicted of conspiracy to commit computer fraud, identity theft, wire fraud, extortion, money laundering, and threats to disclose non-consensual intimate images.

But after watching OpenAI's demo of how ChatGPT handles purchases, and what it does with your bank details, I'm actually feeling a lot less worried.
OpenAI has just launched ChatGPT Wallet. It’s a digital wallet that its agents (called dots) can use to pay for things. They can’t just start buying things willy-nilly though — each payment requires a security check. ChatGPT Wallet has been built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa and currently requires a ChatGPT Pro account in the US to use. La cal del aireador. Cuando el culpable es un único grifo, lo más probable es que la pieza que tiene en la boca, el aireador, se haya ido llenando de cal y otras partículas. Lo mismo pasa si el problema sucede solo en las alcachofas de la ducha.
