India’s deeptech funding record faces a test of scale: Speciale Invest
India’s deeptech funding hit $914 million in 2025, but limited growth capital, manufacturing dependencies and weak commercialisation pathways continue to hinder startups from scaling.
India’s deeptech companies raised $914 million in 257 rounds in 2025, 34 times the 2016 level. The harder test is turning research and prototypes into commercial products, notes Speciale Invest’s report, India’s Deep Tech Revolution - From the Lab to Growth and Exits.
Using Tracxn data through August 31 2026, the study covers 8,293 private companies worldwide, including 482 in India. India accounted for 12.8% of deeptech funding rounds in 2025 but received 1.6% of the capital.
For every 100 seed rounds, India had 23 Series A or B rounds, against 105 globally. Separately, there was one late-stage or private-equity round per 100 Indian seed rounds, against 26 worldwide. Both measures point to funding thinning as companies mature.
Sectoral advantages are uneven. Space firms can tap ISRO testing facilities and suppliers, while life-sciences ventures can draw on India’s pharmaceutical manufacturing base. Private participation in space has widened since 2020 reforms. Registered space startups rose from one in 2014 to about 440 by August 2026.

articles.title: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- In a regulated utility environment, an agentic operations platform keeps reasoning separate from execution: agents correlate signals, assess business impact, and propose remediation, but every production action crosses a deterministic policy boundary that the model cannot override.
- That boundary is defined outside the model. Each proposed action maps to a risk class and approval requirement in a predefined, versioned action catalog, which keeps approval decisions predictable, testable, and reviewable before deployment.
- A governed tool gateway enforces the boundary as the only path from an agent proposal to a production change, with least privilege, independent authorization, approval verification, and complete action evidence attached to that single door.
- Because every action passes through one governed path, the platform produces the evidence needed to support the regulatory and governance requirements of each system, without claiming that the platform itself creates compliance.
- Autonomy is earned rather than assumed: the platform starts read-only and expands one action class at a time, guided by recommendation quality, operator acceptance, execution outcomes, and rollback safety, and that autonomy can be revoked as easily as it is granted.

Esses servidores controlam o acesso aos serviços da empresa (embora não respondam pela autenticação de usuários), recebendo solicitações dos usuários e as encaminhando para os sistemas que devem lidar com elas. Se essa dinâmica falha, os tais serviços deixam de ser acessados.

articles.title: When will humans actually fly on Starship?
articles.summary:
The stunning return of Starship from the skies to a launch tower in South Texas answered some questions about the future of SpaceX’s ambitious rocket program. Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch.
However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle?
The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won’t launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA’s lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth.
Given what is known publicly, and what Ars has heard privately, here are some educated guesses about all of this.
Past is prologue
The first thing we can say for sure is that all estimates of human spaceflight on Starship should be taken with a gigantic grain of salt, including those in this article. Putting humans on any space vehicle is a difficult and time-consuming task, even outside of the requirements that NASA would impose for its astronauts.

articles.title: Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
articles.summary:
Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available.
Natural language search allows guests to describe their preferences in everyday language, such as "romantic cabin near skiing" or "pet-friendly beach house that sleeps eight", rather than relying exclusively on predefined filters. Training such systems presents two challenges: generating queries that reflect actual user behavior and determining which property listings are relevant to each query.
Previous approaches, including InPars and Promptagator, address query generation and relevance labeling as separate tasks. They use LLMs to generate queries from documents or examples, followed by additional model-based judgments to assign relevance labels. According to the researchers, this separation can introduce additional sources of error and differences between synthetic and real-user query distributions.
CASTLE uses contrastive listing pairs derived from de-identified booking sessions. When a guest books a property after viewing several alternatives, the selected listing becomes a positive example, while another viewed but unbooked property serves as a negative example. articles.title: Canadian law firm considering class-action against Microsoft over outage

Frustrated Canadians who experienced problems during a recent Microsoft outage could be part of a potential class-action lawsuit against the tech giant.
Consumer Law Group (CLG), a law firm with offices in Ottawa and Montreal, announced Monday that it is investigating a class-action lawsuit against Microsoft after a global outage affected Microsoft services, including Teams.
The Issue
The outage began on Nov. 12, with hundreds of thousands of North American users reporting issues with Outlook, as well as other services like Teams and Copilot. articles.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place

On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration’s purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government’s actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications.
The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision.
The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn’t bothered to define DEI, and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search.
In the wake of a Supreme Court decision that held that most grant termination cases had to be heard by a different court, the case was narrowed considerably to just seven UC researchers and a handful of agencies: The Environmental Protection Agency, the National Science Foundation, and the National Endowment for the Humanities.

Bon nombre d’entreprises, qui paient pour pouvoir accéder à ces services, se sont retrouvées totalement immobilisées dans leur travail. Comme le rappelle le média américain Wired, Microsoft promet dans ses contrats aux entreprises 99,9 % de disponibilité à ses services par mois. En d’autres termes, sur un mois de 30 jours, seulement 43 minutes d’indisponibilité sont acceptées. Seulement voilà, la panne mondiale qui a touché Outlook, Teams, Copilot et SharePoint les 12 et 13 novembre derniers a duré près de 38 heures (sans parler des répercussions au-delà de Microsoft). This is similar to how the Apple HomeView works, since it also doesn’t use the same technology as Face ID. The HomeView requires you to unlock your smartphone every once in a while for its face unlock to work for security purposes as well.
Also coming to the next developer beta for iOS 27.3 is ‘Close to lock,’ which will let you opt in to lock your device every time you close it. You can find this in Settings, under Display & Brightness.

This JEP proposes a fourth preview, with no changes, after three rounds of preview delivered in the upcoming release of JDK 27 and JDK 26 through JDK 25. articles.title: Microsoft adds a way to remotely lock lost Windows 11 laptops without wiping them
articles.summary:
In context: Windows 11 allows IT administrators to remotely wipe corporate laptops that have been lost or stolen using Microsoft's Intune device management software. Microsoft is now experimenting with a new Remote Locking option designed to protect sensitive data from unauthorized access without deleting any files.
As explained on Microsoft's Learn website, Remote Lock offers a less destructive way to protect data on lost or stolen devices than Remote Wipe. While Remote Wipe deletes all user data from a device, the new feature leaves the data untouched. If the device is recovered, its authorized user can simply sign in and pick up where they left off without losing any files.
When Remote Lock is activated, Windows signs out all active sessions, hides local sign-in options, and displays a custom "Device Locked" screen, preventing users from accessing the device locally or remotely. However, locked devices remain enrolled in and managed through Intune, while BitLocker stays enabled as an additional layer of security.
Remote Lock remains enabled across restarts and while the device is offline. Only an administrator can deactivate it. According to Microsoft, the lock can be lifted only remotely through Intune, as there is no way to unlock the device locally. The company says this restriction is intentional and is designed to prevent malicious actors from using brute-force attacks to gain access to device data.

articles.title: Le chercheur en guerre contre Microsoft dévoile une 16ᵉ faille Windows, elle peut désactiver votre antivirus
articles.summary:
NightmareEclipse a encore frappé. Quelques heures après le Patch Tuesday du 10 novembre, le chercheur Abdelhamid Naceri a mis en ligne une nouvelle faille zero day dans Windows. Baptisée SignDrop, elle permet à un simple utilisateur d’obtenir les droits « SYSTEM », c’est-à-dire les pleins pouvoirs sur l’ordinateur. Comme à son habitude, le chercheur a publié le code d’exploitation sur GitHub, sans prévenir Microsoft en amont, dans le but de mettre la pression sur l’éditeur.
À lire aussi : deux failles de BitLocker permettent de lire les fichiers protégés sur Windows
Une protection de Windows retournée contre lui
Cette fois, le chercheur s’attaque à une protection conçue par Microsoft. La faille se situe dans le CLFS (Common Log File System), un composant clé de Windows qui gère les fichiers journaux du système. Devenu une cible de choix pour les pirates, le composant a eu droit à un mécanisme de protection. L’an dernier, Microsoft a ajouté un système d’authentification, taillé pour signer les fichiers afin de détecter toute modification suspecte.
C’est dans ce système que se trouve la faille SignDrop. Dans les détails, la vulnérabilité pousse Microsoft Defender, l’antivirus par défaut intégré à Windows, à ouvrir un fichier journal (« log ») piégé. Comme Defender dispose des droits les plus élevés du système, Windows crée alors un fichier de signature avec ces mêmes droits, à un emplacement choisi par le pirate. Il n’a plus qu’à y glisser son propre code.

Elastic{ON} Mumbai: Why context, not the model, is the real AI advantage
At Elastic{ON} Mumbai, CEO Ash Kulkarni argued that every business already owns what AI models lack. The rest of the day showed what it takes to put that context to work.
As AI models become available to everyone, the advantage for enterprises is shifting to something no model providers can supply: the context that makes AI useful to a specific business. Elastic{ON} Mumbai took on that challenge, bringing together the people building and running AI in India’s enterprises to work out how to make their data count.
The Elastic{ON} Tour 2026/2027 stopped in Mumbai on September 30, bringing developers, SREs, IT and security leaders and practitioners to JW Marriott Mumbai Sahar under the theme ‘Forge the Future’. Context is your moat

The use of AI agents was found to be close to universal, with 99% of respondents saying they use agents for autonomous or semiautonomous actions in their development pipelines. articles.title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
articles.summary:
Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30.
The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants.
The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period.
In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump.

Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of their seminal book Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was first published. The book updates thinking on site reliability engineering (SRE) to encompass modern cloud architectures, platform engineering and AI workloads, whilst keeping the original emphasis on applying good software engineering techniques to operations work.
Announced by Google's SRE programme manager Betsy Beyer and software engineer David Huska, the new edition is positioned as a response to a production environment that has changed substantially since 2016, when the first edition appeared. The authors argue that the central problem is no longer adopting cloud infrastructure, but maintaining reliability as systems become more distributed, interdependent and continuously changing.
"Modern production environments operate under constant change. System boundaries are more complex, dependencies are deep, and failure modes are more complex and damaging than ever before."
Betsy Beyer and David Huska, Google Cloud Blog
The original SRE book became influential because it gave a public account of how Google operated large-scale services. Plusieurs médias ont déjà remonté le fil de cette infox, qui ne repose sur rien de concret.
Un simple test d’alerte américain
La date vient pourtant d’un exercice bien réel qui aura lieu de l’autre côté de l’Atlantique. Il aura lieu vers 20h20 en France (14h20 heure local), et sera diffusé « uniquement à la radio et à la télévision, sans être envoyé sur les téléphones mobiles », précise la FEMA. Cette dernière ajoute qu’ « aucune action n’est nécessaire de la part du public ». Aucune coupure de courant n’est évidemment prévue, ni aux États-Unis ni ailleurs.
Des comptes spécialisés dans les cryptomonnaies y ont pourtant vu, sans la moindre preuve, l’annonce d’une cyberattaque massive. La rumeur s’est ensuite nourrie d’éléments sortis de leur contexte, comme la recommandation de la Commission européenne de préparer un kit d’urgence pour tenir 72 heures, ou un vieil épisode des Simpson évoquant une panne un 17 novembre. articles.summary:
Overlocker uses vibecoded BIOS modification to target Intel's non-K overclocking restrictions — attempts to revive ASRock's discontinued SkyOC technology
An old ASRock trick gets a second shot.
In an attempt to resurrect ASRock's discontinued SkyOC overclocking feature, an enthusiast has vibe-coded a motherboard BIOS using AI, potentially bringing non-K CPU overclocking to modern Intel CPUs. According to a post on X, Hardware 360º used Chat-GPT Astra to decompile and compare two versions of an ASRock BIOS, one released with SkyOC and another with the feature disabled. The AI reportedly identified the code responsible for enabling the overclocking workaround and modified it to create a BIOS ready for implementation on a compatible motherboard. Unfortunately, it remains to be seen whether the modified firmware can restore SkyOC on modern Intel platforms, as the workaround is yet to be fully tested.
For context, Intel offers multiplier-based overclocking only on its unlocked K-series processors like the Core i9-14900K and the newer Core Ultra 270K Plus. Non-K models have locked multipliers, which restrict users from pushing CPU frequencies. However, there’s another way to raise the speed of a processor by pushing the base clock itself. The base clock, or BCLK, typically runs at 100 MHz and works alongside the CPU multiplier to determine its operating frequency. articles.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.
The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP, a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js, the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.
Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin, as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

The Microsoft 365 outage, which started on Nov. 12 and continued until the morning of Nov. 14, was caused by a combination of issues, including a defect introduced in a July 2026 patch.

First, Lamanna noted that “a latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions.” Notably, Lamanna said the defect was the “result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers” and didn’t impact broader Windows deployments.
The defect was introduced in July, but did not cause any issues until now. Moreover, Lamanna said the defect wasn’t detected by Microsoft’s internal tests, which focused on “weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.” The defect, however, was “worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware.”
The second issue Lamanna highlighted was a surge in load caused by a Teams issue that happened roughly 15 hours before the Microsoft 365 outage. Meta has been ordered to comply within two months, or face an even worse punishment.

The authority eventually concluded that Facebook's behavior was unlawful under Italy's privacy code, which implements Europe's ePrivacy Directive. articles.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
articles.summary:
One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built.
A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward.
Finding the centers
The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts.
In a way, that makes this a very conservative estimate, since 272 facilities believed to be large data centers were left out. But if you’re interested in AI data centers, specifically, it’s also true that some of the facilities included may not fall in that category.

articles.title: Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.
Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.
Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”
In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the new report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes a…

If AI can write the low-level code that ties models to Nvidia, CUDA matters less.
Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding.
Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.

Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.
The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. Initially released a few weeks ago, WinPOPBit is designed to "pop" some of the most restrictive hardware requirements in newer Windows 11 versions. The project is progressing rapidly, which means even more ancient CPUs could soon become "compatible" with the latest PC operating systems.
WinPOPBit primarily targets Windows 11's requirement for CPUs with POPCNT and SSE4.2 instruction support, as well as Windows 10's NX bit requirement. Microsoft introduced the new CPU requirements with the Windows 11 24H2 update, preventing OS enthusiasts from installing the latest release on PCs still running decades-old processors.
Despite acknowledging these new "hard" CPU requirements, WinPOPBit's developers have found a way to restore compatibility. The Python tool is essentially an "experimental patcher" capable of modifying a few relevant bytes in Windows system files, allowing newer OS releases to boot and run on CPUs that date back to before Windows 7 was even a thing.

El invento se llama Cowtainers, que es un juego de palabras entre coworking y containers. No, lo de "cow" no viene por las vacas, aunque en Oviedo no es tan difícil verlas. El proyecto es de Víctor Pérez Arce, arquitecto, y Pablo Díaz Campbell-Smith, ingeniero, dos amigos de la infancia que habían hecho carrera fuera de Asturias y querían volver con algo distinto. La idea llevaba casi cinco años gestándose cuando abrieron, y el coworking está plenamente operativo desde el 30 de junio de 2025. Según cuentan, buena parte de la obra la hicieron ellos mismos, con sus manos. El arranque económico fue un premio de 20.000 euros del programa Entama de EDP, más el apoyo del ayuntamiento de Ribera de Arriba.

articles.title: Las denuncias por material de abuso sexual infantil generado con IA se multiplicaron más de 8.400% en dos años
articles.summary:
Un informe del Childlight Global Child Safety Institute (Instituto Global para la Seguridad Infantil Childlight) revela que las denuncias por abuso sexual infantil en internet pasaron de unas 4.700 en 2023 a más de 400.000 en 2025.
Los reportes de material generado con inteligencia artificial se multiplicaron más de 8.400% en apenas dos años, al pasar de unas 4.700 denuncias en 2023 a más de 400.000 en 2025, según un informe del instituto con sede en Edimburgo. El material incluye imágenes falsas producidas con deepfakes y aplicaciones conocidas como “nudify apps”, que pueden utilizarse para extorsionar a menores y exigirles dinero o más imágenes.
La investigación analizó los reportes que empresas tecnológicas presentaron ante el National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), organismo con sede en Estados Unidos, y se concentró en el este de Asia y el Pacífico, América Latina y el Caribe, y América del Norte. Estudios anteriores del mismo instituto habían examinado la situación en Europa occidental.
Más allá del entorno digital, el informe también relevó datos sobre abuso sexual fuera de línea. En Norteamérica, casi un tercio de las niñas y más de uno de cada diez niños sufrieron abuso sexual presencial durante la infancia, en delitos que incluyen agresión sexual, violación y el llamado “upskirting”. articles.title: TRIUMF: Taking a Tour of Canada’s Particle Accelerator - EE Times
articles.summary:
Canada’s particle accelerator is smaller than CERN’s flagship Large Hadron Collider, but it occupies a distinct place in the international research ecosystem: TRIUMF combines high-intensity beams, rare-isotope production, and specialized materials probes, including capabilities that advance semiconductor research.
Located on the University of British Columbia’s (UBC’s) main, forested campus in Vancouver, the research center was conceived in 1965 as the Tri-University Meson Facility, a joint initiative of UBC, Simon Fraser University, and the University of Victoria. The addition of the University of Alberta as a founding partner soon made the original name less apt. Cyclotron construction began in 1971 and was officially commissioned in 1974. Now the facility is simply known as TRIUMF and is run by a consortium of 21 member universities across Canada.
TRIUMF’s strengths lie in rare‑isotope beams, beta-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β‑NMR), muon spin rotation (μSR), and dedicated nuclear‑astrophysics spectrometers. TRIUMF often contributes specialized detector components, accelerator technology, and computing expertise to large, international experiments, including those at CERN, while its facilities serve as Canada’s main hub for accelerator‑based science and isotope supply.

articles.title: Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
Microsoft has now explained the recent Microsoft 365 outage in a preliminary post-incident report. According to Microsoft, customers were impacted for just under 24 hours, from 4:20 PM UTC on November 12 to 4:10 PM UTC on November 13. The outage prevented many users from accessing their mailboxes in Outlook and delayed email delivery. Moreover, Microsoft Teams, Copilot, SharePoint, and OneDrive were all affected in some way, which is expected since these services all have features that rely on Exchange Online.
The company has traced the outage to three problems that hit Microsoft at the same time. The main culprit is said to be a fix that had been prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 gateway servers. This particular fix, which introduced lock contention in an internal Windows process that exhausted CPU and memory under certain loads, went unnoticed for over three months. That was probably because Microsoft's load testing used weaker machines that couldn't stress the fix properly. Teams also failed over onto the primary gateway it shares with Exchange Online, which worsened the problem. Traffic then shifted to remaining servers, which buckled under the extra load. Apparently, more than 80% of the servers were unresponsive at the worst point of the outage.After that, the recovery process was full of hurdles too. The restored servers were swamped by queued traffic, and the old fix couldn't be hastily undone …

El orquestador. Igual que los modelos MoE (mixture-of-experts) activan solo una parte de sus parámetros según lo que necesitan generar, los orquestadores seleccionan el modelo más adecuado para cada paso de la tarea. Esto es muy útil cuando se genera código, por ejemplo.
En el caso de Anthropic, Claude Code incluye algo parecido con su opusplan. Una vez activo, la herramienta usará Sonnet para la generación de código e implementación, mientras se reserva un modelo superior, Opus, para el modo de planificación. Además, siempre es posible hacerlo “manualmente”: se le puede decir a Codex o a Claude Code que usen un modelo inferior para los pasos de la tarea que requieran ejecución y no razonamiento.

Ese margen de tiempo es el problema que Digitomy, una startup de la Universidad del Sur de Florida (USF), busca eliminar con una trampa que usa inteligencia artificial para dar resultados el mismo día, según informó Fox News.
La urgencia no es teórica. El condado de Hillsborough acumula 407 casos de dengue de transmisión local en 2026, la cifra más alta de su historia.
Las personas afectadas contrajeron el virus dentro del estado, sin haber viajado al exterior. En todo Florida, el número total asciende a 524 casos confirmados hasta el 31 de octubre.

AI agents need more than enterprise data to be effective; they also need the business context that data lives in. Knowledge graphs could consolidate the enterprise context currently fed to different AI agents into a single knowledge layer.
Developers are already providing AI agents with business context through prompts. “This knowledge layer, this idea of capturing your enterprise knowledge and using it as the context engine for your agents, not only gives you the consistency … it gives you the explainability,” he said during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. “That’s the source of my data. These are the elements that I use to produce the answer.”
During interviews at GraphSummit, theCUBE Research’s John Furrier spoke with industry experts from Collibra BV, Blitzy Inc., Raymond James Financial Inc., and Qiagen N.V., among others. Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max with training, attention optimizations
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. today introduced Qwen4-Max, its newest and most capable large language model.
The algorithm not only generates higher-quality output than its predecessor but also costs less. Those improvements are the result of a new architecture, Qwen4, that made the LLM’s training run more efficient. Additionally, Alibaba has equipped the model with an upgraded attention mechanism.
Qwen4-Max’s backbone, the part of an LLM that functions as its main processing engine, comprises 2.4 trillion parameters. The model activates only 71 billion at any given time. The backbone is supported by 328 billion so-called N-gram parameters, which function as a kind of cache. They save the results of oft-repeated calculations and thereby remove the need to compute them from scratch every time.
An LLM’s artificial neurons are organized into sets known as layers. When the model learns something new during training, a piece of data called a gradient travels through the layers and refines their output. The gradient moves through them one by one starting from the last layer, which finalizes and displays prompt responses.
Qwen4-Max includes a feature that enables the gradient to skip some layers. That feature, or residual, is effectively a shortcut inside the LLM. Its purpose is to reduce errors during the training workflow, which in turn lowers costs and improves output quality.

articles.title: Noeri raises $110M to help companies build living AI systems that self-improve over time - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Noeri raises $110M to help companies build living AI systems that self-improve over time
Noeri Inc., a startup developing artificial intelligence systems that continuously improve their outputs as they learn from an organization’s data and work, is launching with $110 million in funding.
Today’s round was led by Menlo Ventures and saw participation from Seattle-based Madrona Ventures, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Snowflake and Cisco Ventures also took part in the round.
Noeri is the brainchild of Yejin Choi (pictured, left) and Carlos Guestrin (right), two prominent AI researchers from Stanford University, who spent years developing self-improving systems at the University of Washington prior to moving. The startup’s software is designed to study a company’s data, workflows and business processes.
Then as it learns about them, it will begin to propose changes regarding specific tasks, in order to make them more efficient. The co-founders refer to it as a “living” AI system that gets better at what it does over time.
For instance, it might offer different instructions, suggest different tools or switch out the model that handles each step of a workflow for another. Each of these suggestions comes with an explanation and is sent to a human for review before it’s accepted, similar to how AI-generated code changes are implemented.

articles.title: En 1919, Nueva York levantó dos pirámides con 12.000 cascos alemanes. Alguien tenía que pagar la factura de la Primera Guerra Mundial
articles.summary:
En la primavera de 1919, miles de neoyorquinos que salían de Grand Central Terminal se encontraron con una imagen insólita. Park Avenue había dejado de parecer una de las grandes avenidas de Manhattan para convertirse en una monumental exposición de armamento alemán. La Primera Guerra Mundial había terminado cinco meses antes, pero Estados Unidos todavía tenía un problema gigantesco por resolver.
La guerra había terminado, la factura no. El armisticio del 11 de noviembre de 1918 había puesto fin a los combates de la Primera Guerra Mundial, pero no a sus consecuencias económicas. Estados Unidos todavía necesitaba miles de millones de dólares para sufragar los gastos militares, mantener a sus tropas en Europa y repatriar a cientos de miles de soldados.
Para conseguirlos, el Gobierno lanzó en abril de 1919 su quinta gran campaña de financiación de la guerra, denominada Victory Liberty Loan, con el objetivo de recaudar 4.500 millones de dólares. Y en Nueva York tuvieron una idea extraordinaria para convencer a los ciudadanos de que prestaran su dinero al Estado: utilizar los restos del ejército que acababan de derrotar.
Una pirámide de cascos alemanes. El general John J. Pershing, comandante de las fuerzas expedicionarias estadounidenses en Europa, envió 12.000 cascos militares alemanes a Nueva York. China retains fastest supercomputer in the world crown as AI data centers soak up new hardware — Top500 records fewest new systems in 33 years
As hyperscalers want more AI, traditional supercomputers take a back seat.
China's LineShine remains the world's highest-performing supercomputer, according to the 68th edition of the Top500 list published at SC26 in Chicago on Monday. For the first time in decades, the supercomputer ranking saw exceptionally few additions despite unprecedented demand for high-performance computing hardware, as the vast amounts of compute resources deployed these days are destined for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers rather than traditional supercomputers.
Top 10 supercomputers unchanged
China's LineShine, installed at the National Supercomputer Center in Shenzhen, offers sustained FP64 compute performance of 2.198 FP64 ExaFLOPS in the High Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark at 42.22 MW. The machine relies on the homegrown LingKun platform with 304-core Armx9-based LX2 processors clocked at 1.55 GHz (13,789,440 cores in total) and the proprietary LingQi interconnect. Unlike the other four exascale-class supercomputers, LineShine does not use any compute accelerators and exclusively relies on CPUs, which is largely why it only gains 3.6X performance when moving from FP64 to mixed-precision data, which is lower than systems that use low-precision accelerators.

Monday, November 16th 2026
ORICO Introduces FlashMem FM9800 SSDs with Dedicated AI Cache
Chinese peripherals company ORICO introduced the FlashMem AI SSD FM9800. The M.2 drive uses a graphene thermal pad, PCIe 5.0 interface and 3D TLC NAND. It will be available in 1 TB and 2 TB models, fairly standard for this type of drive. However, the drive splits its capacity between two areas (partitions) combining regular storage with a dedicated cache area for local AI. Storage OS area holds the operating system, applications, and regular files. The so-called AI Cache stores data used for local AI inference. The 1 TB model allocates 85 GB to AI Cache and 768 GB to Storage OS. The 2 TB version reserves 128 GB for AI Cache and 1,638 GB for Storage OS. ORICO has not explained how the remaining capacity is allocated, with over-provisioning being an option.
According to the company, the two areas use separate wear-management strategies and read/write scheduling. ORICO intends the AI Cache to work alongside system RAM and GPU memory. Moreover, compatible applications could use it as an additional storage layer for local AI. It does not replace RAM or VRAM, and software support will be needed to use the feature. ORICO has yet to share exact performance or endurance ratings. However, an additional image from ORICO's blog post advertises read speeds of up to 9,800 MB/s. Warranty details, availability, and pricing are also unknown.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 Cuts Overhead with On-Demand XWayland Implementation
articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
KDE Plasma 6.9 Cuts Overhead with On-Demand XWayland Implementation
KDE Plasma is one of the most commonly recommended Linux desktop environments, thanks to its flexibility, frequent updates, and surprisingly low performance footprint. According to the latest issue of This Week in Plasma by KDE's Nate Graham, KDE Plasma 6.9 will introduce a more streamlined implementation of XWayland. 
The big change would enable XWayland—the compatibility layer that enables compatibility with legacy X11 apps—to run on-demand. That is to say that XWayland will only run when the user or system launch an application that requires the compatibility layer, as opposed to running in the background all the time.Other notable mentions include speed improvements for both the KDE screenshot utility, Spectacle, and for the Add Widgets sidebar on the desktop. The KDE Login Manager also now includes an automatic terminal fallback when it fails. Several customization and settings pages have also received small tweaks that make them more intuitive to use more visually appealing. The network widget also now includes an option to forget networks, instead of making users open the setting app to do it, and the System Monitor app and widgets also include a sensor to list physical CPU cores.

articles.title: Linux Kernel Gets AMD Capacity-Aware Scheduling for Zen 6 Heterogeneous CPU Architectures
articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Linux Kernel Gets AMD Capacity-Aware Scheduling for Zen 6 Heterogeneous CPU Architectures
It has long been rumored that AMD is working on new Zen 6 LP cores for its next-gen Zen 6 (see our Zen 6 Technical Deep Dive here) CPU architecture—which has already been unveiled for server applications—and it now appears as though the Linux kernel is being prepared to support that new architecture across the board. A patch series by AMD itself details support for a Capacity-Aware Scheduling, which would effectively allow the Linux kernel to detect the capabilities of each individual CPU core and assign work to that CPU core accordingly.
Amd-pstate does not export per-CPU capacity today, so the scheduler treats all cores as equal and places tasks without regard to core strength.
Patch 1 makes amd-pstate publish asymmetric per-CPU capacities via the arch hybrid capacity scaling interface. It is enabled by default on supported hardware and can be turned off with the "amd_cas=disable" boot parameter.
Patch 2 makes amd-hfi stand down when CAS is active, since both manage the same scheduler state.
Capacity-aware scheduling would enable Capacity-Aware Scheduling on all AMD heterogeneous CPUs on Linux, which means going back to certain CPUs in the Hawk Point family, which combined Zen 4 and Zen 4c CPUs. articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Overclocker Tries to Revive SkyOC BCLK Overclocking via BIOS Mod
Back in 2015, ASRock introduced SkyOC, a feature that let users overclock locked non-K series Intel CPUs via BCLK overclocking. That BIOS trick might be making an unofficial comeback, thanks to a decompilation attempt by Spanish creator Hardware 360°. He posted on X about a modified BIOS that he had built for his ASUS ROG Maximus XI Extreme Z390 motherboard with the help of AI tools. That modified BIOS ports the SkyOC feature from ASRock motherboards of the time, using firmware from before and after ASRock pulled the plug on it. Apparently, Intel was not happy about BCLK overclocking on Skylake CPUs using SkyOC.
The idea behind this modified BIOS is to let non-K Intel CPUs be overclocked using BCLK without destabilizing the entire system. Typically, BCLK overclocking raises the clocks for the entire motherboard, including RAM, PCIe buses, etc. Therefore, Intel implemented a limit on BCLK, so that the CPUs shut down if they detected a BCLK higher than 103 MHz (up from 100 MHz). SkyOC got around this limit by feeding the CPU a false BCLK reading, which is why Intel directed ASRock to remove this feature in early 2016 with a microcode update. articles.title: AMD is adding tamper-resistant hardware to its chips to protect from physical attacks
articles.summary:
AMD is adding tamper-resistant hardware to its chips to protect from physical attacks
AMD is building backside protection into the silicon
- AMD's Versal TR adaptive SoCs bond a sensor die to the silicon backside that detects physical attacks and blocks boot if removed
- Post-quantum ML-DSA and SLH-DSA acceleration arrives after rivals Altera and Lattice already shipped post-quantum secure boot
- Samples are not due until the second half of 2027, and AMD itself says tamper-resistant does not mean tamper-proof
AMD has unveiled a family of adaptive chips with their own built-in bodyguard.
The company's new Versal tamper-resistant devices bond a sensor-based protection die to the back of the main compute die, where it shields the silicon, watches for physical attacks, and stops the chip from booting if it is tampered with or removed.
The chips, specifically the 2VE3358TR, 2VE3558TR and 2VE3858TR, are all variants of the Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs that AMD first unveiled alongside Arm in 2024, and will look to cater to the likes of defense systems, data center networking, financial technology and critical industrial infrastructure.
A second die guarding the side that nobody watches?
One might ponder why the backside is suddenly important: most high-performance chips are flip-chip packaged, mounted face down, so the transistors sit against the package while the bare silicon substrate faces up.

articles.title: L'institut de sondages Ipsos confirme une intrusion dans son système informatique

Le géant français des sondages Ipsos a été victime d’une cyberattaque contre l’un de ses systèmes informatiques internes, et il a attendu cinq jours après le dépôt de sa plainte pour l’annoncer. Le groupe ignore encore si des informations sur ses clients ont été touchées.
Avec environ 20 000 salariés et 5 000 clients dans 90 pays, Ipsos réalise des sondages d’opinion et des études de marché pour des entreprises, des médias et des institutions. Dans son communiqué, le groupe explique avoir identifié « un incident de cybersécurité affectant un système d’information interne » et porté plainte le 11 novembre. Ses équipes ont déclenché les procédures de réponse aux incidents et fait appel à des spécialistes extérieurs pour contenir l’attaque. Selon l’entreprise, celle-ci n’a eu « aucun impact » sur ses opérations. Lo dijo en un discurso en Milán.
Barr habló ante la conferencia anual de la Asociación de Maquinaria de Computación (ACM) sobre IA en las finanzas. Explicó que esos asistentes, llamados agentes de IA, son programas que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta, como mover dinero o hacer compras en nombre de una persona.
El gobernador no nombró a los bancos ni dio cifras de incidentes. Según el texto de su discurso, publicado por la Reserva Federal, las entidades informan de estos intentos, y los controles se vuelven más urgentes a medida que se extiende el comercio con agentes, es decir, las compras que hacen los asistentes de IA por los usuarios.
Para Barr, el servicio solo funcionará a largo plazo con controles. Pidió autenticación estricta, verificación explícita del consentimiento para cada acción concreta, límites técnicos a lo que puede hacer un agente y reglas que obliguen a estos programas a respetar normas y valores.
Una corrida bancaria que se produzca en minutos
El segundo riesgo que planteó afecta a la estabilidad del sistema. Hasta ahora, un cliente tenía que ordenar cada transferencia. Un agente de IA, en cambio, podría detectar diferencias de rendimiento entre cuentas o señales de inesta…

Weekend project
The AWS team, using a clearly defined specification, instructed its Kiro autonomous agent with a simple prompt – and were surprised by the results.
Although not an emulator in the strictest sense, the AWS Emulator provides a useful local platform to help developers become confident that their code will run effectively when uploaded to the real AWS.
The prompt used to develop the AWS Emulator began life one weekend as a three-step instruction essentially to test Sr. Principal Engineer Matthew Goldberg’s initial hypothesis.
The agent would perform write tests the AWS Command Line Interface, and iterate on the tests until they can pass on the real AWS. When that was achieved, the agent would then assemble an implementation that the tests would pass with.

articles.title: Crean un sensor portátil que podría detectar químicos eternos en el agua: cómo funciona

El agua puede parecer limpia y contener rastros de sustancias conocidas como químicos eternos, que persisten durante décadas. Para identificarlas sin depender siempre de un laboratorio, el Instituto de Ciencia y Tecnología de Okinawa (Japón) creó un sensor portátil capaz de detectar PFAS en agua.
El desafío es llevar el análisis al lugar donde se toma la muestra. Los métodos habituales son precisos, pero requieren equipos especializados, trasladar las muestras y contar con instrumentos costosos. El prototipo propone una primera medición con una tira flexible conectada a un aparato de lectura.
El dispositivo se ensayó con PFOA y PFOS, dos compuestos de la familia de las PFAS, en agua potable y dulce. El avance se describe en un estudio publicado en la revista Biosensors and Bioelectronics. Vale destacar que se trata de resultados iniciales y aún necesitan validación en otras condiciones ambientales.
Las PFAS persisten y por eso resulta difícil vigilar su presencia
Las sustancias perfluoroalquiladas y polifluoroalquiladas, conocidas como PFAS, se usan en materiales resistentes al agua, el aceite y el calor. Esa resistencia también dificulta que se degraden, por lo que pueden acumularse en el agua, el suelo y los organismos, según el comunicado del instituto.
El estudio abordó la detección de dos de esos compuestos en concentraciones muy bajas con una herramienta que pueda trasladarse. Para ello, el equipo fabricó nanopartículas de polímeros de impresión molecular, un material d…

Active since at least 2023, BO Team focuses on cyber espionage and hacktivism, and has a history of targeting Russian entities to steal valuable data and break into compromised infrastructure using tools like Mythic and Cobalt Strike, along with its own malware such as BrockenDoor and ZeronetKit. articles.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
articles.summary:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.
The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.
The team said this week that it cannot verify the outcomes reported by the agents. It has moderate confidence that the agents ran on ARTEX, an open-source AI tool for penetration testing.
The records include a playbook of known entry points for each targeted product. It lists default administrator credentials such as LiteLLM's default master key, unfinished installs that an outsider could take over, and known flaws in Langflow and RAGFlow.
In a separate case reported this week, Cloudflare's incident responders saw ARTEX gain access to a compromised API token that had been used for CI/CD. The token had no IP restrictions or rate limiting, and the activity that followed included 400 database dump requests in an hour. The company has not said whether those requests returned any data.
An operator gives ARTEX a target and a goal, and a planner agent splits the goal into tasks for worker agents that run security tools. To decide each next step, the agents send their work to a large language model (LLM).

articles.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
articles.summary:
A financially motivated threat activity cluster tracked as REF3364 has been attributed to a Linux-focused cryptocurrency mining operation that tampers with the readings used to detect high GPU workloads.
Central to the intrusion is a toolkit called SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator that receives commands over the TOR anonymity network to manage CPU and GPU miners. The activity was observed in late October 2026.
"The threat actor also deployed a kernel rootkit to hide selected processes and files, an NVIDIA Management Library (NVML) wrapper to falsify GPU readings, and a separate backdoor named netns," Elastic Security Labs said in a report published last week.
"This backdoor retrieves its C2 [command-and-control] address from an Ethereum smart contract before connecting to the server directly."
In the attack chain documented by the company, initial access is said to have been achieved via an exposed Ray job agent, allowing the threat actor to execute commands. This includes jobs running the NVIDIA System Management Interface (nvidia-smi) to capture and exfiltrate the GPU inventory to an external server.
Subsequently, the attacker submitted a Python reverse shell job that connected to a remote listener, after which an SSH key was added to that account's authorized_keys file to establish persistent access.

articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new variant of CoffeeLoader, a malware designed to deliver additional payloads to infected machines.
"On launch, the NSIS-based installer executable dropped a file named '7z.dll' into a temporary directory and ran it through rundll32.exe," Kaspersky said in an analysis published today.
"The '7z.dll' file was a patched version of the original library of the popular 7-Zip archiver. Part of its code had been replaced with malicious self-decrypting shellcode that turned out to be a new version of the Armoury packer."
CoffeeLoader was first documented by Zscaler ThreatLabz in March 2025, detailing its use of the Armoury packer to resist analysis and ultimately run Rhadamanthys shellcode. The malware is assessed to share source code similarities with another loader family tracked as SmokeLoader.
Malware packed with Armory uses file names like "ArmouryAIOSDK.dll" and "ArmouryA.dll," with the packer hijacking some of the original Armoury Crate functionality with self-decrypting shellcode.
Notably, the shellcode extracts code that executes a decryption routine on a system's GPU by making use of the OpenCL library. The end goal is to install CoffeeLoader, establish persistence, and execute it by injecting it into a newly created "dllhost.exe" process.

Six flaws in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers could let a remote attacker take over a controller without logging in, Dutch security consultancy Midnight Blue said earlier this week.
No patch is available, and the researchers say the newest firmware, version 5.4.0, does not fix the flaws.
Government cybersecurity agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany told operators this week to take the controllers' management interfaces off the internet.
For a controller left on the internet, updating the firmware, changing default passwords or turning on Strict mode is not enough on its own, the Belgian and Irish agencies said. Strict mode is a login protection that requires encrypted connections and session tokens, but one of the six flaws is in the gateway that enforces it.
The AK-SM800A runs a store's fridges and freezers, and maintenance firms can manage it remotely. Such controllers were targeted in attacks in France starting October 11, and in a second wave across Europe that began last week. The attacks caused unwanted defrost cycles and destroyed stock.
Germany's federal IT security agency, the BSI, says in a security notice that the AK-SM800A was involved in earlier incidents in which refrigeration units in several countries were tampered with.
The agency has no information about any exploitation of the six new flaws, and neither other agencies nor researchers link the flaws to those incidents.

Chaque ordre devrait être validé par le commissaire au renseignement. Certains fournisseurs pourraient aussi devoir garder des métadonnées jusqu’à six mois. articles.title: Unos 400 centros de datos de Estados Unidos usan casi tanta electricidad como todo el estado de Michigan

Un grupo de 403 centros de datos de gran tamaño en Estados Unidos consumió entre 68 y 99 teravatios-hora de electricidad en un año, una cifra cuyo extremo alto se acerca al consumo anual de estados como Michigan, según un estudio de la Universidad de Harvard publicado el 16 de noviembre en la revista Nature Sustainability.
El equipo, liderado por el investigador Gianluca Guidi, estudió las instalaciones que operaron entre mayo de 2024 y abril de 2025. Son los llamados centros de datos de hiperescala: los más grandes, que pertenecen a las mayores empresas de computación en la nube y de inteligencia artificial. Su capacidad promedio es de unos 40 megavatios.
En su escenario central, estos centros usaron unos 82 teravatios-hora, equivalentes a cerca del 1,8% de toda la electricidad que consume el país. Las emisiones de dióxido de carbono asociadas fueron de unos 25,7 millones de toneladas, de dos a tres veces más que una estimación anterior para 2018, según el comunicado de Harvard.
Más de la mitad de la energía es fósil
Alrededor del 54% de la electricidad que alimenta a estos centros se generó con combustibles fósiles: 38% con gas natural y 15% con carbón. Además, cerca de una cuarta parte de la energía se consumió en regiones cuya red eléctrica emite más carbono que el promedio nacional.
El consumo se concentra en pocos lugares. Virginia, Oregon, Ohio e Iowa reúnen más de la mitad de la electricidad analizada, según los investigadores. Virginia aloja la zona conocida como Dat…

articles.title: Google Finds Hackers Using AI Agents to Build and Run Exploits From Software Patches
articles.summary:
Google on Monday revealed that adversarial use of artificial intelligence (AI) by threat actors has gone beyond manual prompting to deploying autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks like ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI to execute multi-stage intrusions at greater operational velocity.
In tandem, threat actors are leveraging the power and capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and agentic frameworks to automate the reverse engineering of patches via differential analysis, allowing them to rapidly weaponize newly disclosed vulnerabilities, as observed in the case of PaperCut NG/MF flaws earlier this September.
The abuse of open source, agentic penetration-testing (pentesting) frameworks is seen as a way to "automate discrete phases and specific operational tasks during live intrusions," Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
The tech giant said the adoption represents a paradigm shift in which cyber attacks take place at machine speed, allowing the operations to be scaled significantly by chaining together varied attack paths even if the underlying mechanics remain the same.
A number of threat actors have been observed experimenting with these frameworks and harnesses, including financially motivated and suspected espionage actors aligned with China.

articles.title: iOS 27.3 : Apple ajoute une reconnaissance faciale inédite à l'iPhone Duo
articles.summary:
L’iPhone Duo va bientôt pouvoir se déverrouiller d’un simple regard sans pour autant bénéficier du véritable Face ID. Avec la deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3, Apple introduit aussi une option attendue par certains utilisateurs : le verrouillage automatique du smartphone lorsqu’ils le referment.
Jusqu’ici, les utilisateurs de l'iPhone Duo devaient passer par Touch ID ou saisir leur code pour déverrouiller leur appareil. La deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3 change quelque peu la donne en introduisant une nouvelle méthode d’authentification basée sur la caméra frontale située sur l’écran extérieur.
L’iPhone Duo peut désormais reconnaître le visage de son propriétaire
Une fois l’option activée dans les réglages, depuis le menu « Touch ID et code », le smartphone peut reconnaître le visage de son propriétaire pour autoriser son déverrouillage lorsqu’il est fermé. Apple précise néanmoins qu’une authentification récente par Touch ID ou avec le code reste nécessaire pour activer cette fonction. Les données de reconnaissance faciale restent quant à elles stockées sur l'appareil.
Attention toutefois, il ne s’agit pas d’une arrivée de Face ID sur l’iPhone Duo. Le smartphone ne dispose pas des composants nécessaires au fonctionnement du système de reconnaissance faciale d’Apple. Cette nouveauté repose uniquement sur la caméra frontale et présente donc des restrictions plus importantes.
En effet, la reconnaissance faciale ne sert ici qu’à déverrouiller le téléphone. Pour effectuer un paiement avec Apple …

articles.title: "Quiero que la gente tenga mucha RAM, todos deberían poder comprarla para su propia computadora": Sam Altman de OpenAI
articles.summary:
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, dijo que quiere que todas las personas puedan comprar mucha memoria RAM para sus computadoras. Lo afirmó en una cumbre de Semafor en San Francisco, donde reconoció que el precio de este componente subió entre cinco y siete veces.
“Quiero ser claro: quiero que la gente tenga mucha RAM, creo que todos deberían poder comprar mucha RAM para su propia computadora”, afirmó Altman, según The Verge. Agregó que “el trabajo casero de experimentación es genial”.
Sobre el aumento de precios, dijo que “los precios de la DRAM, no sé exactamente, quizá subieron cinco veces, siete veces, algo así”. La DRAM es el tipo de memoria que usan las computadoras y los teléfonos para ejecutar programas. Altman admitió que no conocía la cifra exacta.
El ejecutivo sostuvo que desde hace años pide ampliar la cadena de suministro de memoria y que el mundo no construyó suficiente capacidad. También señaló que OpenAI estuvo limitada en distintos momentos por la memoria, el armado de servidores, la capacidad de los centros de datos o “algún componente aleatorio”.
La polémica que Altman intenta cerrar
Todo comenzó en el pódcast Cheeky Pint, conducido por John Collison, cofundador de la empresa de pagos Stripe. En una entrevista publicada el 29 de octubre, según el portal Cognizec, Altman dijo que es “bastante terrible” que cada persona tenga parte del suministro limitado de DRAM en su computadora, usada “el cinco por ciento del tiempo”.

articles.title: N-able Patches 17 N-central Flaws as Attackers Exploit Earlier Bugs to Deploy Crypto Miners
articles.summary:
N-able has released a new security update to address additional critical security flaws impacting N-central.
Describing N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 as a critical security update, the company said it includes a number of security patches and fixes that enhance the security of the Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) and Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform.
"HF3 builds on the protections delivered in HF2 and includes further improvements across authentication and access controls, Agent and Probe communications, file handling, server components, legacy APIs, and user management," the company said.
The improvements relate to authentication and access control; Agent, Probe, and appliance security; file and import handling; server hardening; and user management controls. As part of the change, the configuration option for legacy APIs has been completely removed, permanently blocking them.
As of writing, N-able notes that both Remote control functionality and Intune integration are blocked.
Customers running on-premise N-central deployments should upgrade their servers as soon as possible to keep their environments protected. For Hosted N-central servers, no server-side action is required, as the updates are being automatically applied.
"All customers, hosted and on-premise, must upgrade all of their Agents and Probes to the latest version to be fully protected," N-able cautioned. "Agents and Probes that are not upgraded are susceptible to impersonation."

articles.title: El hacker que filtró 90 videos de GTA VI se declaró culpable tres días antes del lanzamiento del juego
articles.summary:
Arion Kurtaj, el joven británico de 21 años que en 2022 filtró 90 videos del videojuego Grand Theft Auto VI, se declaró culpable ante el Tribunal de la Corona de Woolwich, en Londres. Admitió además ataques informáticos contra otras empresas. Será sentenciado el 23 de noviembre.
Según la Fiscalía de la Corona del Reino Unido (CPS), Kurtaj integraba el grupo de ciberdelincuentes Lapsus$. Reconoció los ataques a Rockstar Games, la desarrolladora del juego, y a la operadora de telefonía BT/EE, la empresa de pagos Revolut y la plataforma de transporte Uber.
Los cargos incluyen tres delitos de actos no autorizados que perjudican el funcionamiento de un sistema informático, uno de fraude y uno de acceso no autorizado con intención de cometer otro delito, según The Independent. También admitió haber tenido un teléfono móvil dentro de la cárcel.
El lanzamiento de GTA VI está previsto para el 19 de noviembre. La declaración de culpabilidad llega, así, tres días antes del estreno de un título que la propia filtración de Kurtaj mostró al mundo mucho antes de su presentación oficial.
Un hackeo con un televisor de hotel y un Fire Stick
Kurtaj estaba en libertad bajo fianza por otros ataques cuando atacó a Rockstar. Lo habían alojado en un hotel de Bicester, en Oxfordshire, para protegerlo de hackers rivales, según la BBC. Sin su computadora, que le habían confiscado, usó un Fire Stick de Amazon conectado al televisor del cuarto, además de un teclado y un ratón inalámbricos.

articles.title: Brave nettoie maintenant les trackers des photos de Facebook et Instagram
articles.summary:
Depuis sa version 1.98 pour ordinateur, Brave efface automatiquement le marqueur « FBMD » que Meta ajoute aux images publiées sur Facebook et Instagram. Invisible à l’écran, ce code suit la photo partout où elle va et pourrait relier des comptes que leurs propriétaires voulaient garder séparés.
Parmi les métadonnées intégrées à une photo, on retrouve la date, l’heure, la position GPS ou le modèle de l’appareil, des informations cachées que n’importe quel site ou application peut lire. Brave s'attaque à l'une d'elles, ajoutée par Meta.
FBMD, le code qui voyage avec la photo
Meta ajoute cette métadonnée dans un champ défini par l’IPTC, l’organisme qui fixe les standards de la presse (légendes, crédits, copyright). L’IPTC a mené un test sur les métadonnées des photos publiées sur Facebook. Meta supprime la plupart d’entre elles, mais ajoute une valeur dans le champ “Special Instructions”. Cette dernière commence par “FBMD”, suivie d’une longue suite de caractères. Et elle reste identique quand quelqu’un télécharge l’image pour la republier. Brave a refait le test en juillet 2026 et ce marqueur est toujours bel et bien là.
Prenons un exemple. Un internaute engagé dans une association tient un compte Instagram sous un pseudonyme. Ce compte est séparé de son profil Facebook à son nom, que suivent sa famille et ses collègues. Elle utilise une adresse e-mail dédiée, voire un VPN. ConnectWise on Monday said it completed its investigation into unauthorized access targeting partner ScreenConnect environments, and recommended customers to ensure that the technician client is running version 26.6.5 or later.
The company said additional activity targeting on-premises environments continues to be reported where the identified third-party extensions remain enabled, and ScreenConnect has not been updated to the latest version.
"On-premises partners must immediately disable the identified extensions and update ScreenConnect to the latest supported version," the company said.
It's worth noting that version 26.6.5 addresses a critical-severity flaw in ScreenConnect client tracked as CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9) that could allow files to be transferred and executed through an active remote session without authorization or Host confirmation in certain circumstances.
As highlighted by Huntress and Blackpoint Cyber last week, unknown threat actors are suspected to be exploiting an authentication flaw in RMM+ versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 to execute unauthorized commands while bypassing ScreenConnect's regular authentication controls.
The attacks have been found to deploy a multi-component toolkit dubbed SCKit that's capable of spreading from infected customer devices to MSP technicians' computers and compromising additional managed networks by means of a C# module called RelayTrap ("RelayTrap.cs").

articles.title: Hijacked Optimizely Scripts Served Card Skimmer and iOS Exploit Kits to CNN, BBC and Zoom Visitors
articles.summary:
An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation to plant malicious code in some of the scripts that customers' websites load from the service, Optimizely said early today.
Visitors to sites run by at least 178 organizations, including CNN, the BBC and Zoom, received the code yesterday, according to Report URI, a firm that monitors the scripts websites run.
The code was built to replace crypto wallet addresses with the attacker's own addresses and to capture card details, but the firm cannot see how many card numbers were exposed to the attacker. The vendor says it has fixed the flaw and removed the code.
On iPhones and iPads, the code was also set up to load a second stage that the firm identifies as an iOS exploit kit, but it reports no iPhones actually being taken over.
In an incident notice posted at 01:02 UTC, Optimizely said the attacker had "exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation" and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.
The vendor has also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and added protections to stop unauthorized code from being delivered. The notice does not say how the flaw worked, how many projects were changed, when the fix went in, whether the attacker still has any access, or what customers should do.
Smartsheet's script was cleaned once and then re-infected with a hidden version of the code, which indicates the attacker still had access at that point, according to the firm.

articles.title: Un error de julio que nadie detectó causó la caída de Microsoft 365 que duró casi 24 horas
articles.summary:
Microsoft informó que un defecto de software instalado en julio, y que ninguna prueba detectó, provocó la caída mundial de Microsoft 365 del 12 de noviembre de 2026. El fallo dejó sin respuesta a más del 80% de los servidores de acceso y afectó a Outlook, Teams y Copilot durante casi 24 horas.
La empresa explicó la causa en un informe preliminar que publicó para sus clientes en el centro de administración de Microsoft 365. Charles Lamanna, vicepresidente ejecutivo de Copilot, agentes y plataforma, difundió un resumen en la red social X y pidió disculpas: “Lamentamos profundamente el impacto para todos nuestros clientes”.
Según el informe, la caída comenzó a las 16:20 (hora universal) del 12 de noviembre y los servicios quedaron restablecidos a las 16:10 del día siguiente, según BleepingComputer y Ars Technica. Microsoft sostiene que se trató de un problema técnico sin relación con un ciberataque ni con agentes de IA.
Tres problemas que coincidieron
El primero fue el defecto, que formaba parte de una actualización diseñada para los servidores que funcionan como puerta de entrada a Microsoft 365. Esa actualización empezó a instalarse en julio y funcionó en todo el mundo durante más de tres meses sin incidentes, según la compañía.
El error hacía que un servidor se saturara y dejara de responder cuando se juntaban ciertas condiciones de tráfico. Microsoft dijo que sus pruebas de carga no lo detectaron porque se hicieron sobre equipos más débiles, con menos núcleos de procesamient…

articles.title: Apple sera jugé en juin 2027 en France pour des soupçons d'obsolescence programmée
articles.summary:
Apple doit comparaître devant le tribunal correctionnel de Paris en juin 2027 pour des entraves présumées à la réparation des iPhone. La procédure vise les restrictions logicielles qui peuvent limiter certaines fonctions après le remplacement d’une pièce hors de son réseau agréé.
Changer une batterie ou un écran devrait permettre de prolonger la vie d’un smartphone. Mais lorsque le logiciel s’en mêle, une pièce de remplacement ne suffit pas toujours à retrouver un appareil pleinement fonctionnel. C’est ce mécanisme qui sera au cœur du prochain procès d’Apple en France, après une plainte déposée en décembre 2022 par l’association Halte à l’obsolescence programmée, ou HOP.
Un procès prévu en juin, une première audience dès le mois de février
C’est l’association elle-même qui annonce dans un communiqué qu’une audience de fixation se tiendra le 25 février 2027, avant plusieurs jours de plaidoiries en juin. L’association précise que sa plainte concerne 24 modèles d’iPhone. Son dossier de presse situe la période incriminée entre le 17 novembre 2021 et le 23 juillet 2024.
Cette étape donne une suite concrète à la plainte déposée contre Apple en 2022, puis à l’enquête sur ses pratiques de réparation. Le tribunal devra déterminer si les restrictions reprochées constituent des infractions. À ce stade, aucune condamnation n’a été prononcée dans ce dossier.

articles.title: California demandó a OpenAI por agentes de IA que escaparon de una prueba y hackearon a otra empresa
articles.summary:
El fiscal general de California, Rob Bonta, demandó a OpenAI, la creadora de ChatGPT, por probar modelos de IA sin controles suficientes. Según la demanda, centenares de agentes de IA escaparon de su entorno de pruebas en julio y atacaron durante dos días y medio a la plataforma Hugging Face.
Los agentes son asistentes de IA que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta. Hugging Face es un sitio abierto donde desarrolladores de todo el mundo publican y descargan modelos de IA. La demanda se presentó en el Tribunal Superior de San Francisco contra OpenAI Foundation y OpenAI Group PBC.
La fiscalía acusa a la empresa de crear una molestia pública que pone en peligro la seguridad de la población y de violar la ley californiana de competencia desleal, que prohíbe las prácticas comerciales ilegales, injustas o fraudulentas. Según Bloomberg Law, el estado pide una orden judicial, USD 2.500 por cada infracción y la devolución de ganancias.
Bonta dijo en una conferencia de prensa que OpenAI admitió ante sus investigadores que perdió el control de sus agentes al menos 80 veces durante pruebas. Agregó que la empresa no entregó la información detallada que se le pidió para evaluar esos casos, algo que, afirmó, “pone en riesgo al público”.

El texto judicial describe una cadena de fallas. Entre mayo y junio, OpenAI hizo pruebas de entrenamiento en entornos aislados, con acceso a un servicio de paquetes de software alojado en sus propios servidores. Como var…

articles.title: OVHcloud lance Olala, son premier modèle d'IA maison entraîné sur des supercalculateurs européens
articles.summary:
Avec Olala mini 7A1B, OVHcloud fait son entrée sur le marché des modèles de langage. Entraînée de zéro grâce à des supercalculateurs européens, cette nouvelle IA française mise sur une architecture économe en ressources, et a déjà trouvé sa place chez Qwant.
L'Europe veut réduire sa dépendance aux géants américains de l'intelligence artificielle, et OVHcloud compte bien prendre part à l'effort. Alors que le groupe français mettait jusqu'ici ses infrastructures cloud à la disposition de ses clients pour entraîner et faire tourner leurs modèles d'IA, il passe désormais de l'autre côté du miroir en concevant le sien. Dévoilé ce mardi 17 novembre, Olala mini 7A1B inaugure une famille de LLM maison qui entend offrir aux entreprises européennes une alternative aux modèles d'OpenAI, de Google ou de Meta.
Un modèle compact, capable de fonctionner sans carte graphique
Pour son premier LLM, OVHcloud a misé sur une architecture conçue pour limiter les ressources nécessaires à son fonctionnement et faciliter son déploiement sur des machines moins puissantes. Olala mini compte ainsi sept milliards de paramètres, mais n'en mobilise qu'un milliard à la fois, grâce à une architecture dite Mixture of Experts (MoE), ou mélange d'experts, dont le principe consiste à répartir le traitement des requêtes entre des groupes de paramètres spécialisés, au lieu de solliciter l'ensemble du modèle pour chaque réponse.

articles.title: Ingeniería y neurociencia: así es la pulsera que nació en el MIT y hoy ayuda a controlar temblores en decenas de pacientes
articles.summary:
La Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos (FDA) de Estados Unidos autorizó, a comienzos de 2026, una pulsera de la empresa de neurotecnología Encora Therapeutics para ayudar a adultos con temblor esencial, un trastorno que provoca sacudidas frecuentes en las manos y puede dificultar tareas cotidianas.
Más allá del avance, el dispositivo cuenta con una historia muy particular: fue desarrollado a partir de un proyecto estudiantil del Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT), aplica vibraciones mecánicas en la muñeca para enviar señales al cerebro y reducir los movimientos involuntarios, informó MIT News, el portal de noticias del instituto.
La autorización llegó en febrero, 9 años después de que un hombre con Parkinson de inicio temprano probara un prototipo ante un auditorio lleno en el MIT. Al activar la vibración, pudo dibujar una espiral con una precisión muy superior a la que tenía segundos antes.
En ensayos posteriores, una prueba de uso domiciliario durante 90 días mostró que el 78% de los pacientes informó beneficios. Con base en el conjunto de la evidencia clínica, el dispositivo obtuvo la autorización 510(k) de la FDA, un mecanismo regulatorio que certifica que el aparato es seguro y equivalente en eficacia a otros dispositivos ya aprobados en el mercado.

Over half of businesses admit they're facing significantly higher AI costs than they expected
Token costs down, AI bills up
- Financial costs of AI are now a cause of concern for over 50% of executives
- While token cost is a concern, related expenditure such as training and governance is also having an impact
- Few organizations are able to link AI use to related business outcomes, leaving them struggling to justify increasing expenditure
AI expenditure is busting budgets, even with a decrease in token costs for the most popular AI models, new Capgemini research has claimed.
The research shows over half (53%) of executives are concerned about AI costs, with expenditure on tokens, training, governance, and supplemental spending on human oversight and repeated work all contributing to the uncertainty.
Meanwhile, 59% of execs have reported that their expected AI related expenditure was surpassed, with 20% of organizations breaching their AI budget target by over 30%. Consequently, according to the report, more businesses are finding that CFOs are increasingly involved in AI spending decisions.

500 CXO-level senior executives working at large organizations were polled during September 2026, with the report highlighting the growing financial burden of AI.
